1|INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community|"# INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community

The community centers on the relationship between the INSURER and the INSURED PERSON, with the INSURANCE POLICY as the governing contract. The policy is structured into three main coverage parts: Part I-Liability to Others, Part II-Medical Payments Coverage, and Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage. Various entities such as RELATIVE, LIABLE PARTY, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and ATTOTNEY interact with these core parties, creating a network of rights, obligations, and potential disputes. The community is characterized by complex legal and financial relationships, with the INSURER holding rights of recovery and the INSURED PERSON entitled to benefits but also subject to reimbursement and cooperation requirements. The presence of arbitration, financial responsibility laws, and material misrepresentation clauses adds layers of regulatory and legal significance.

## Central relationship between INSURER and INSURED PERSON

The INSURER and INSURED PERSON form the core of the insurance community. The INSURER provides financial protection, makes payments on behalf of the insured, and retains rights of recovery and reimbursement. The INSURED PERSON is entitled to benefits such as medical payments and liability coverage, but must also cooperate with the insurer, sign documents, and reimburse payments from liable parties. This relationship is fundamental to the operation of the policy and underlies all other interactions. [Data: Entities (71, 68); Relationships (90, 77, 120, 122, 310, 318, 319, +more)]

## Insurance policy structure and coverage parts

The INSURANCE POLICY is the contract that binds the parties and is divided into three main parts. Part I-Liability to Others covers the insured's liability to third parties, with the insurer's duty to pay contingent on a final determination of the insured's obligation. Part II-Medical Payments Coverage provides for medical expenses due to bodily injury from auto accidents. Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage addresses situations where the other driver is uninsured or underinsured, and may reduce payments under Part I. These parts define the scope of coverage and the conditions under which benefits are paid. [Data: Entities (75, 3, 83, 84, 85); Relationships (106, 158, 18, 19, +more)]

## DEFINITIONS OF LIABLE PARTY AND RECOVERY RIGHTS

The LIABLE PARTY is an entity or individual legally or financially obligated to make payments to an insured person. The insured person may recover from the liable party, and such amounts are held in trust for the insurer. The INSURER holds RECOVERY RIGHTS to the extent of its payments, and the insured must assist in exercising these rights. This dynamic creates a triangular relationship where the insurer seeks reimbursement from the liable party, often requiring the insured's cooperation. [Data: Entities (181, 187, 188); Relationships (310, 319, 320)]

## ROLE OF MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS AND ATTORNEYS

MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS deliver medical services and may sue the insured person if the insurer refuses to pay for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. They may also pursue collection activities. ATTORNEYS represent insured persons in recovering payments from liable parties, with fees shared pro rata by the insurer. These entities introduce potential legal disputes and financial obligations that can escalate the complexity of claims. [Data: Entities (88, 182); Relationships (135, 312)]

## RELATIVE AND RATED RESIDENT AS INSURED PERSONS

A RELATIVE is defined as a family member related by blood, marriage, or adoption, and may qualify as an insured person under the policy, particularly for accidents arising from the ownership, maintenance, or use of an auto. A RATED RESIDENT is included within the definition of an insured person and is covered for auto-related accidents. However, coverage can be affected by factors such as the relative's driver's license status, vehicle ownership or regular use, and intentional acts. These entities expand the scope of who is protected under the policy. [Data: Entities (63, 68); Relationships (77, 110)]

## ARBITRATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

ARBITRATION is a subsection of Part III and is used to determine the legal liability of the operator or owner of an uninsured motor vehicle and the amount of damages sustained by the insured person. Each party selects an arbitrator, and the two arbitrators select a third. The court may appoint the third arbitrator on joint application. This mechanism provides an alternative to litigation for resolving disputes related to uninsured or underinsured motorist claims. [Data: Entities (26, 103, 104); Relationships (34, 167, 166)]

## MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION AND CANCELLATION

MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION is a misrepresentation of a material fact in the procurement, continuation, change, or renewal of the policy, or in the submission of a claim, which constitutes grounds for cancellation after 59 days. This clause protects the insurer from fraud and ensures that the policy is based on accurate information. The insured person's obligation to provide truthful information is thus critical to maintaining coverage. [Data: Entities (173, 184, 70); Relationships (277, 314, 315)]

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS AND OTHER LEGAL REQUIREMENTS

FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS are a subsection of Part I-Liability to Others and mandate that individuals demonstrate the ability to cover damages arising from vehicle accidents, typically through insurance. A policy complies with these laws when properly certified. Additionally, sums paid under workers' compensation or disability benefits laws reduce the limits of liability under Part III. These legal requirements ensure that insured persons meet statutory obligations and that the insurer's liability is coordinated with other sources of compensation. [Data: Entities (21, 99, 100); Relationships (126, 161, 162)]"

39|INSURER and the Insurance Policy Ecosystem|"# INSURER and the Insurance Policy Ecosystem

This community is centered on the INSURER, the underwriting company that provides insurance coverage and is the central party in the insurance relationship. The INSURER is bound by a complex web of relationships with the INSURED PERSON, the INSURANCE POLICY, and various service providers such as NON-OWNED AUTO, RENTAL AGENCY, AUTO REPAIR SHOP, and SERVICE CENTERS. The INSURER holds rights of recovery and settlement and bears obligations as set forth in the policy. Key entities include the INSURANCE POLICY, which is the contract of insurance, and CLAIM, which refers to submissions under the policy and claims for damages. The community also involves RESPONSIBLE PARTY, from whom the insurer may seek reimbursement, and SALVAGE, property retained by the insurer. The relationships highlight the insurer's role in providing financial protection, making payments, and managing claims, while reserving rights to pursue liable parties. This ecosystem is essential for understanding the flow of obligations, coverage, and potential risks such as fraud.

## INSURER as the Central Entity

The INSURER is the underwriting company that provides insurance coverage and is identified on the declarations page as 'we,' 'us,' and 'our.' It is responsible for making payments under the policy, holds rights of recovery and settlement, and bears various obligations. The INSURER is also an entity that may benefit from sums excluded under the policy. With a degree of 17, it is the most connected entity in this community, linking to the INSURED PERSON, INSURANCE POLICY, NON-OWNED AUTO, RESPONSIBLE PARTY, RENTAL AGENCY, AUTO REPAIR SHOP, and SERVICE CENTERS. This central position underscores its pivotal role in the insurance ecosystem, as it both provides financial protection and seeks reimbursement from liable parties. [Data: Entities (71); Relationships (90, 107, 180, 337, 182, 183, 184, +more)]

## INSURANCE POLICY as the Contractual Framework

The INSURANCE POLICY is the contract of insurance between the insured and the insurer, including the declarations page, definitions, and coverage parts. It is provided by the INSURER, as indicated by the relationship 'The insurance policy is provided by the insurer.' The policy also governs the retention of salvage, with the stipulation that if the insurer retains salvage under the policy, it has no duty to preserve it. This entity is fundamental as it defines the terms, conditions, and scope of coverage, serving as the legal backbone of the insurance relationship. [Data: Entities (75); Relationships (107, 304)]

## Relationship Between INSURER and INSURED PERSON

The relationship between the INSURER and the INSURED PERSON is characterized by the insurer providing financial protection and making payments on behalf of the insured. The insurer makes payments to or on behalf of the insured person and seeks reimbursement from liable parties. Additionally, the insurer pays damages for bodily injury and property damage for which an insured person becomes legally responsible. The insurer also pays for covered losses and reimburses expenses of the insured person. This relationship, with a combined degree of 57, is the strongest in the community, highlighting the core function of insurance: transferring risk from the insured to the insurer in exchange for premiums. [Data: Relationships (90)]

## Coverage for NON-OWNED AUTO

The INSURER provides collision and comprehensive coverage for a NON-OWNED AUTO, which is a vehicle not owned by the insured but covered under the policy. This coverage is essential for situations where the insured may rent or borrow a vehicle. The relationship 'The insurer provides collision and comprehensive coverage for the non-owned auto' (combined degree 19) indicates the insurer's obligation to extend coverage beyond owned vehicles, thereby broadening the scope of protection and potential liability. [Data: Entities (110); Relationships (180)]

## Claims Against RESPONSIBLE PARTY

The INSURER reserves the right to compromise or settle deductible and property damage claims against a RESPONSIBLE PARTY, who is a party responsible for a loss or damage. This relationship (combined degree 19) is crucial for the insurer's subrogation efforts, allowing it to recover payments made to the insured from liable third parties. This process helps mitigate the insurer's financial exposure and can impact the overall cost of insurance. [Data: Entities (190); Relationships (337)]

## Reimbursement for RENTAL AGENCY and AUTO REPAIR SHOP

The INSURER reimburses rental charges incurred when the insured rents from a RENTAL AGENCY and also reimburses rental charges incurred from an AUTO REPAIR SHOP, where covered autos may be delivered for repairs. These relationships (combined degrees 18 each) illustrate the insurer's role in covering ancillary expenses related to vehicle loss or damage. By reimbursing rental costs, the insurer ensures that the insured maintains mobility while their vehicle is being repaired or replaced. [Data: Entities (111, 112); Relationships (182, 183)]

## Insurer-Operated SERVICE CENTERS

The INSURER operates SERVICE CENTERS where covered autos can be delivered for repairs. This relationship (combined degree 18) indicates that the insurer may directly manage repair facilities, potentially streamlining the claims process, controlling costs, and ensuring quality of repairs. The existence of service centers also reflects the insurer's vertical integration in the auto insurance sector. [Data: Entities (108); Relationships (184)]

## CLAIM and Fraud Implications

The term CLAIM refers to two distinct concepts: a submission made under the policy in which material misrepresentation or fraud constitutes grounds for cancellation, and any claim for damages covered by Part I that the insurer will settle or defend at its option. The relationship 'Fraud in the submission of any claim under the policy is grounds for cancellation' (combined degree 6) highlights the serious consequences of fraudulent claims. Fraud can lead to policy cancellation and potentially legal action, posing a significant risk to both the insurer and the insured. [Data: Entities (70); Relationships (315)]

## SALVAGE and Insurer's Rights

SALVAGE refers to property retained by the insurer, which has no duty to preserve it for any purpose including evidence. This relationship (combined degree 14) indicates that the insurer may take possession of damaged property after settling a claim, but is not obligated to maintain it. This can have implications for disputes over evidence or value, and underscores the insurer's rights in the claims process. [Data: Entities (178); Relationships (304)]"

## MAINE AUTO POLICY

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

## GENERAL DEFINITIONS

The following definitions apply throughout the policy . Defined terms are printed in boldface type and have the same meaning whether in the singular, plural, or any other form.

- 1 . ' Additional auto ' means an auto you become the owner of during the policy period that does not permanently replace an auto shown on the declarations page
- if:
- a. we insure all other autos you own;
- b. the additional auto is not covered by any other insurance policy;
- c. you notify us within 30 days of becoming the owner of the additional auto ; and
- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

2. ' Auto ' means a land motor vehicle:
- a. of the private passenger, pickup body,

- a. unpaid finance charges or refunds due to the owner for such charges;
- b. excess mileage charges or charges for wear and tear;
- c. charges for extended warranties or refunds due to the owner for extended warranties;
- d. charges for credit insurance or refunds due to the owner for credit insurance;
- e. past due payments and charges for past due payments; and
- f. collection or repossession expenses.

However, our payment under this coverage shall not exceed the limit of liability shown on the declarations page .   The limit of liability is a percentage of the actual cash value of the covered auto at the time of the loss.

This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-PET INJURY COVERAGE

If you have purchased Collision coverage for at least one covered auto under your policy , and if your pet sustains injury or death while inside a covered auto or nonowned auto at the time of a loss covered under Collision or Comprehensive coverage, we will provide:

- 1 . up to $1,000 for reasonable and customary veterinary fees incurred by you , a relative , or a rated resident if your pet is injured in, or as a direct result of, the covered loss; or
2. a $1,000 death benefit if your pet dies in, or as a direct result of, the covered loss, less any payment we made toward veterinary expenses for your pet .

In the event of a covered loss due to the theft of a covered auto or non-owned auto , we will provide the death benefit provided your pet is inside that auto at the time of the theft and your pet is not recovered.

## ADDITIONAL DEFINITIONS

When used in this Part IV:

- 1 . ' Collision ' means the upset of a vehicle or its impact with another vehicle or object.
2. ' Custom  parts  or  equipment '  means  equipment,  devices,  accessories,  enhancements and changes, other than those that are offered by the manufacturer specifically for that auto model, or that are installed by the auto dealership as part

- of the original sale of a new auto , that:
- a. are permanently installed or attached; and
- b. alter the appearance or performance of the auto .
3. ' Mechanical parts ' means operational parts on a vehicle that wear out over time or have a finite useful life or duration typically shorter than the life of the vehicle as a whole. Mechanical parts do not include external crash parts, wheels, paint, or windshields and other glass.
4. ' Non-owned auto ' means an auto that is not owned by or furnished or available for the regular use of you , a relative , or a rated resident while in the custody of or being operated by you , a relative , or a rated resident with the permission of the owner of the auto or the person in lawful possession of the auto .
5. ' Your pet ' means any dog or cat owned by you , a relative , or a rated resident .

## EXCLUSIONS-READ THE FOLLOWING EXCLUSIONS CAREFULLY. IF AN EXCLUSION APPLIES, COVERAGE WILL NOT BE AFFORDED UNDER THIS PART IV.

Coverage under this Part IV will not apply for loss:

- 1 . to any vehicle while being used:
- a. to carry persons or property for compensation or a fee;
- b. for retail or wholesale delivery , including, but not limited to, the pickup, transport or delivery of magazines, newspapers, mail or food; or
- c. for ride-sharing activity .

This exclusion does not apply to shared-expense car pools;

2. to a non-owned auto while being maintained or used by a person while employed or engaged in any auto business ;
3. to any vehicle resulting from, or sustained during practice or preparation for:

4. to any vehicle for which insurance:

6. to a covered auto while it is leased or rented to others or given in exchange for compensation, including while being used in connection with a personal vehicle sharing program .  This exclusion does not apply to the operation of a covered auto by you , a relative , or a rated resident ;

## PAYMENT OF LOSS

We may, at our option:

- 1 . pay for the loss in money; or
2. repair or replace the damaged or stolen property.

At our expense, we may return any recovered stolen property to you or to the address shown on the declarations page , with payment for any damage resulting from the theft. We may keep all or part of the property at the agreed or appraised value.

We may settle any loss with you or the owner or lienholder of the property .

## NO BENEFIT TO BAILEE

Coverage under this Part IV will not directly or indirectly benefit any carrier or other bailee for hire.

## LOSS PAYABLE CLAUSE

Payment under this Part IV for a loss to a covered auto will be made according to your interest and the interest of any lienholder shown on the declarations page or designated by you .  At our option, payment may be made to both jointly, or to either separately. However, if the covered auto is not a total loss, we may make payment to you and the repairer of the auto .

The lienholder's interest will not be protected:

- 1 . where fraud, misrepresentation, material omission, or intentional damage resulting in a denial of coverage by us has been committed by or at the direction of you or any person seeking coverage; or
2. where the loss is otherwise not covered under the terms of this policy .

If this policy is cancelled, nonrenewed or voided, the interest of any lienholder under this agreement will also terminate.

## OTHER SOURCES OF RECOVERY

If other sources of recovery also cover the loss, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable

limits. However, any insurance we provide for a non-owned auto , or trailer not shown on the declarations page , will be excess over any other collectible source of recovery including, but not limited to:

- 1 . any coverage provided by the owner of the non-owned auto or trailer ;
2. any other applicable physical damage insurance; and
3. any other source of recovery applicable to the loss.

## APPRAISAL

If we cannot agree with you on the amount of a loss, then we or you may demand an appraisal of the loss. Within 30 days of any demand for an appraisal, each party shall appoint a competent appraiser and shall notify the other party of that appraiser's identity . The appraisers will determine the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, the disagreement will be submitted to a qualified umpire chosen by the appraisers. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days, we or you may request that a judge of a court of record, in the county where you reside, select an umpire. The appraisers and umpire will determine the amount of loss. The amount of loss agreed to by both appraisers, or by one appraiser and the umpire, will be binding. You will pay your appraiser's fees and expenses. We will pay our appraiser's fees and expenses. All other expenses of the appraisal, including payment of the umpire if one is selected, will be shared equally between us and you .   Neither we nor you waive any rights under this policy by agreeing to an appraisal.

## PART IV-DAMAGE TO A VEHICLE

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COLLISION COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , resulting from collision .

In addition, we will pay the reasonable cost to replace any child safety seat damaged in an accident to which this coverage applies.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;
2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;
3. when the auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

5. if the loss is theft of a rented non-owned auto , 30 days after loss of use begins on the loss.

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-ADDITIONAL CUSTOM PARTS OR EQUIPMENT COVERAGE

We will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to custom parts or equipment on a covered auto for which this coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages. This coverage applies in addition to any coverage automatically provided for custom parts or equipment under Comprehensive Coverage or Collision Coverage.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-RENTAL REIMBURSEMENT COVERAGE

We will reimburse rental charges incurred when you rent an auto from a rental agency or auto repair shop due to a loss to a covered auto for which Rental Reimbursement Coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages.

## MAINE AUTO POLICY

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

## GENERAL DEFINITIONS

The following definitions apply throughout the policy . Defined terms are printed in boldface type and have the same meaning whether in the singular, plural, or any other form.

- 1 . ' Additional auto ' means an auto you become the owner of during the policy period that does not permanently replace an auto shown on the declarations page
- if:
- a. we insure all other autos you own;
- b. the additional auto is not covered by any other insurance policy;
- c. you notify us within 30 days of becoming the owner of the additional auto ; and
- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

2. ' Auto ' means a land motor vehicle:

We will not make an adjustment for the labor costs associated with the replacement or repair of these parts.

- g. The actual cash value of a vehicle equals its replacement cost at the time the loss occurs, less the value of its physical depreciation as determined by standard business practices.
3. We will not pay for loss of use of a rental vehicle for more than 30 days.
4. No deductible will apply to a loss to window glass when the glass is repaired instead of replaced.

5. Duplicate recovery for the same elements of damages is not permitted.
6. The following additional limits of liability apply to Pet Injury coverage:
- a. The most we will pay for all damages in any one loss is a total of $1,000 regardless of the number of dogs or cats involved.
- b. If your pet dies in, or as a direct result of, a covered loss, we will provide a death benefit of $1,000, less any payment we made toward veterinary expenses for your pet .
- c. No deductible shall apply to this coverage.

## PAYMENT OF LOSS

We may, at our option:

- 1 . pay for the loss in money; or
2. repair or replace the damaged or stolen property.

At our expense, we may return any recovered stolen property to you or to the address shown on the declarations page , with payment for any damage resulting from the theft. We may keep all or part of the property at the agreed or appraised value.

We may settle any loss with you or the owner or lienholder of the property .

## NO BENEFIT TO BAILEE

Coverage under this Part IV will not directly or indirectly benefit any carrier or other bailee for hire.

## LOSS PAYABLE CLAUSE

Payment under this Part IV for a loss to a covered auto will be made according to your interest and the interest of any lienholder shown on the declarations page or designated by you .  At our option, payment may be made to both jointly, or to either separately. However, if the covered auto is not a total loss, we may make payment to you and the repairer of the auto .

The lienholder's interest will not be protected:

- 1 . where fraud, misrepresentation, material omission, or intentional damage resulting in a denial of coverage by us has been committed by or at the direction of you or any person seeking coverage; or
2. where the loss is otherwise not covered under the terms of this policy .

If this policy is cancelled, nonrenewed or voided, the interest of any lienholder under this agreement will also terminate.

## OTHER SOURCES OF RECOVERY

If other sources of recovery also cover the loss, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable

limits. However, any insurance we provide for a non-owned auto , or trailer not shown on the declarations page , will be excess over any other collectible source of recovery including, but not limited to:

- 1 . any coverage provided by the owner of the non-owned auto or trailer ;
2. any other applicable physical damage insurance; and
3. any other source of recovery applicable to the loss.

## APPRAISAL

If we cannot agree with you on the amount of a loss, then we or you may demand an appraisal of the loss. Within 30 days of any demand for an appraisal, each party shall appoint a competent appraiser and shall notify the other party of that appraiser's identity . The appraisers will determine the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, the disagreement will be submitted to a qualified umpire chosen by the appraisers. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days, we or you may request that a judge of a court of record, in the county where you reside, select an umpire. The appraisers and umpire will determine the amount of loss. The amount of loss agreed to by both appraisers, or by one appraiser and the umpire, will be binding. You will pay your appraiser's fees and expenses. We will pay our appraiser's fees and expenses. All other expenses of the appraisal, including payment of the umpire if one is selected, will be shared equally between us and you .   Neither we nor you waive any rights under this policy by agreeing to an appraisal.

When service is rendered by a provider in the business of providing roadside assistance and towing services, other than one of our authorized service representatives, we will pay only reasonable charges, as determined by us , for:

which is necessary due to a covered emergency

## PART VI-DUTIES IN CASE OF AN ACCIDENT OR LOSS

For coverage to apply under this policy, you or  the  person seeking coverage must promptly report each accident or loss even if you or the person seeking coverage is not

You or the person seeking coverage must also obtain and provide us the names and addresses of all persons involved in the accident or loss, the names and addresses of any witnesses, and the license plate numbers of the vehicles involved.

If you or the person seeking coverage cannot identify the owner or operator of a vehicle involved in the accident, or if theft or vandalism has occurred, you or the person seeking coverage must notify the police within 24 hours or as soon as practicable.

- 7 . allow us to have the damaged covered auto , or any other damaged vehicle for which coverage is sought, inspected and appraised before its repair or disposal;
8. submit to medical examinations at our expense by doctors we select as often as we may reasonably require; and
9. authorize us to obtain medical and other records.

5|Roadside Assistance Coverage under Part V|"# Roadside Assistance Coverage under Part V

The community centers on Part V of an insurance policy, which provides roadside assistance coverage. Key entities include Covered Disabled Auto, Covered Emergency, Authorized Service Representative, and exclusions for unauthorized service providers and certain facilities. The relationships define the conditions for coverage, the services provided, and the limitations. This community is important for understanding the scope and limitations of roadside assistance insurance, affecting policyholders, insurers, and service providers.

## Part V and Roadside Assistance Coverage

Part V of the insurance policy is dedicated to roadside assistance coverage, which includes towing and labor services for covered disabled autos. This section is a critical component of the policy, providing essential services during emergencies. The coverage is triggered by a covered emergency and is subject to specific conditions and exclusions. [Data: Entities (137, 138); Relationships (211)]

## Definition of Covered Emergency

A covered emergency is defined as a disablement arising from mechanical or electrical breakdown, battery failure, insufficient fluid supply, flat tire, accidental lock-out, or entrapment in snow, mud, water, or sand within 100 feet of a road or highway. This broad definition ensures that various common roadside issues are covered, but it also sets clear boundaries, such as the distance limitation for entrapment. [Data: Entities (146); Relationships (221, 222)]

## Covered Disabled Auto

A covered disabled auto is a covered auto that sustains a covered emergency. This entity is central to the coverage, as it links the vehicle to the emergency event that triggers the roadside assistance services. The coverage is contingent on the auto being covered under the policy and the emergency meeting the defined criteria. [Data: Entities (145); Relationships (221)]

## Authorized Service Representative

An authorized service representative is a service representative authorized by the insurer to provide towing and labor services under Part V. This entity ensures that services are rendered by approved providers, which may affect reimbursement and quality of service. The relationship between the representative and the coverage highlights the importance of using authorized personnel. [Data: Entities (144); Relationships (218)]

## Unauthorized Service Provider Subsection

Part V contains a subsection addressing unauthorized service providers, which likely outlines the consequences of using non-authorized services, such as denial of coverage or reduced reimbursement. This subsection is important for policyholders to understand to avoid unexpected out-of-pocket expenses. [Data: Entities (38); Relationships (51)]

## Exclusions for Service Stations, Garages, and Repair Shops

Labor or repair work performed at a service station, garage, or repair shop is excluded from coverage. These exclusions prevent coverage for routine repairs or maintenance, focusing the coverage on emergency roadside assistance. Policyholders should be aware that work done at these facilities is not covered. [Data: Entities (151, 152, 153); Relationships (235, 236, 237)]

## Part VI and Duties After an Accident or Loss

Part VI of the policy describes duties in case of an accident or loss, including the requirement to protect the covered auto from further loss. This part is related to the roadside assistance coverage as it sets out obligations that may affect claims. The relationship between Part VI and Covered Disabled Auto shows that policyholders must take certain actions to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (148); Relationships (227)]"

A "COVERED AUTO" refers to any vehicle insured under an insurance policy for which certain exclusions do not apply and coverage is provided. This designation encompasses a range of vehicles, including those specifically listed or defined in the policy, and is subject to various exclusions and limits. For instance, collision and comprehensive coverage may apply to a covered auto, including an attached trailer.

More specifically, a covered auto includes any auto or trailer shown on the declarations page, any additional auto, any replacement auto, or a trailer owned by the insured. These vehicles are explicitly identified or defined within the insurance policy, ensuring that coverage is extended to them while remaining subject to the policy's terms, conditions, and limitations.

In essence, a covered auto is a vehicle that qualifies for insurance protection under the policy, whether listed on the declarations page, added later, or serving as a replacement, as well as any trailer owned by the insured. ## PAYMENT OF LOSS

We may, at our option:

- 1 . pay for the loss in money; or
2. repair or replace the damaged or stolen property.

At our expense, we may return any recovered stolen property to you or to the address shown on the declarations page , with payment for any damage resulting from the theft. We may keep all or part of the property at the agreed or appraised value.

We may settle any loss with you or the owner or lienholder of the property .

## NO BENEFIT TO BAILEE

Coverage under this Part IV will not directly or indirectly benefit any carrier or other bailee for hire.

## LOSS PAYABLE CLAUSE

Payment under this Part IV for a loss to a covered auto will be made according to your interest and the interest of any lienholder shown on the declarations page or designated by you .  At our option, payment may be made to both jointly, or to either separately. However, if the covered auto is not a total loss, we may make payment to you and the repairer of the auto .

The lienholder's interest will not be protected:

- 1 . where fraud, misrepresentation, material omission, or intentional damage resulting in a denial of coverage by us has been committed by or at the direction of you or any person seeking coverage; or
2. where the loss is otherwise not covered under the terms of this policy .

If this policy is cancelled, nonrenewed or voided, the interest of any lienholder under this agreement will also terminate.

## OTHER SOURCES OF RECOVERY

If other sources of recovery also cover the loss, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable

limits. However, any insurance we provide for a non-owned auto , or trailer not shown on the declarations page , will be excess over any other collectible source of recovery including, but not limited to:

- 1 . any coverage provided by the owner of the non-owned auto or trailer ;
2. any other applicable physical damage insurance; and
3. any other source of recovery applicable to the loss.

## APPRAISAL

If we cannot agree with you on the amount of a loss, then we or you may demand an appraisal of the loss. Within 30 days of any demand for an appraisal, each party shall appoint a competent appraiser and shall notify the other party of that appraiser's identity . The appraisers will determine the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, the disagreement will be submitted to a qualified umpire chosen by the appraisers. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days, we or you may request that a judge of a court of record, in the county where you reside, select an umpire. The appraisers and umpire will determine the amount of loss. The amount of loss agreed to by both appraisers, or by one appraiser and the umpire, will be binding. You will pay your appraiser's fees and expenses. We will pay our appraiser's fees and expenses. All other expenses of the appraisal, including payment of the umpire if one is selected, will be shared equally between us and you .   Neither we nor you waive any rights under this policy by agreeing to an appraisal.

## INSURING AGREEMENT

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . We will insure you for the coverages and the limits of liability shown on this policy's declarations page . Your policy consists of the policy contract, your insurance application, the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy .

## GENERAL DEFINITIONS

- d. you pay any additional premium due.

An additional auto will have the broadest coverage we provide for any auto shown on the declarations page .  If you ask us to insure an additional auto more than 30 days after you become the owner, any coverage we provide will begin at the time you request coverage.

2. ' Auto ' means a land motor vehicle:

## PAYMENT OF LOSS

We may, at our option:

- 1 . pay for the loss in money; or

## NO BENEFIT TO BAILEE

Coverage under this Part IV will not directly or indirectly benefit any carrier or other bailee for hire.

## LOSS PAYABLE CLAUSE

Payment under this Part IV for a loss to a covered auto will be made according to your interest and the interest of any lienholder shown on the declarations page or designated by you .  At our option, payment may be made to both jointly, or to either separately. However, if the covered auto is not a total loss, we may make payment to you and the repairer of the auto .

The lienholder's interest will not be protected:

- 1 . where fraud, misrepresentation, material omission, or intentional damage resulting in a denial of coverage by us has been committed by or at the direction of you or any person seeking coverage; or
2. where the loss is otherwise not covered under the terms of this policy .

If this policy is cancelled, nonrenewed or voided, the interest of any lienholder under this agreement will also terminate.

## OTHER SOURCES OF RECOVERY

If other sources of recovery also cover the loss, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable

limits. However, any insurance we provide for a non-owned auto , or trailer not shown on the declarations page , will be excess over any other collectible source of recovery including, but not limited to:

- 1 . any coverage provided by the owner of the non-owned auto or trailer ;
2. any other applicable physical damage insurance; and
3. any other source of recovery applicable to the loss.

## APPRAISAL

If we cannot agree with you on the amount of a loss, then we or you may demand an appraisal of the loss. Within 30 days of any demand for an appraisal, each party shall appoint a competent appraiser and shall notify the other party of that appraiser's identity . The appraisers will determine the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, the disagreement will be submitted to a qualified umpire chosen by the appraisers. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days, we or you may request that a judge of a court of record, in the county where you reside, select an umpire. The appraisers and umpire will determine the amount of loss. The amount of loss agreed to by both appraisers, or by one appraiser and the umpire, will be binding. You will pay your appraiser's fees and expenses. We will pay our appraiser's fees and expenses. All other expenses of the appraisal, including payment of the umpire if one is selected, will be shared equally between us and you . This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

7|Maine Auto Policy and Its Coverage Structure|"# Maine Auto Policy and Its Coverage Structure

The community is centered on the Maine Auto Policy, a comprehensive auto insurance policy issued in Maine. It comprises multiple coverage parts: Part II (Medical Payments), Part III (Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist), Part IV (Damage to a Vehicle), Part V (Roadside Assistance), and Part VI (Duties in Case of Accident or Loss). Part IV is the most detailed, containing numerous insuring agreements for collision, comprehensive, custom parts, rental reimbursement, loan/lease payoff, and pet injury, along with payment of loss, no benefit to bailee, loss payable clause, and other sources of recovery. Common subsections such as Exclusions, Other Insurance, Additional Definitions, and Limits of Liability appear across multiple parts. The policy is governed by a Policy Contract that includes the insurance application and endorsements.

## Centrality of Part IV-Damage to a Vehicle

Part IV-Damage to a Vehicle is the most connected entity in the community, with a degree of 17, indicating its central role in the policy structure. It encompasses various coverage types, including collision, comprehensive, custom parts, rental reimbursement, loan/lease payoff, and pet injury, each addressed in separate insuring agreements. This part also includes subsections on payment of loss, no benefit to bailee, loss payable clause, and other sources of recovery, making it a comprehensive section for vehicle damage claims. Exclusions specify what is not covered, while Other Insurance addresses coordination with other policies. Additional Definitions provide clarity on terms, and Limits of Liability set maximum payment amounts. These recurring subsections ensure consistency and comprehensiveness across different coverage parts, helping to avoid ambiguity and manage risk. This structure ensures that the policyholder and insurer have a clear understanding of their rights and obligations, with endorsements allowing for modifications to the standard policy. The contract's components are essential for legal enforcement and claims resolution. [Data: Entities (16, 13, 15, 1); Relationships (12, 13, 15)]

The Maine Auto Policy is specifically applicable in the state of Maine, as indicated by its relationship with the entity 'MAINE'. Notably, it addresses reimbursement to the insurer contingent on a signed reimbursement agreement and the insurer's pro rata share of attorney fees. Part VI-DUTIES IN CASE OF AN ACCIDENT OR LOSS outlines the policyholder's obligations following an accident or loss, such as promptly notifying the insurer, cooperating in the investigation, and submitting proof of loss. Upon cancellation, you may be entitled to a premium refund. However, our making or offering of a refund is not a condition of cancellation.

## NONRENEWAL

If neither we nor one of our affiliates offers to renew or continue this policy , we will mail notice of nonrenewal to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records. A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. ## AUTOMATIC TERMINATION

If we or an affiliate offers to renew or continue this policy and you or your representative does not accept, this policy will automatically terminate at the end of the current policy period. Failure to pay the required renewal or continuation premium when due will mean that you have not accepted our offer.

If you obtain other insurance on a covered auto , any similar insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the other insurance.

If a covered auto is sold or transferred to someone other than you or a relative , any insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the sale or transfer.

1|INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community|"# INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community

The community centers on the relationship between the INSURER and the INSURED PERSON, with the INSURANCE POLICY as the governing contract. The policy is structured into three main coverage parts: Part I-Liability to Others, Part II-Medical Payments Coverage, and Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage. Various entities such as RELATIVE, LIABLE PARTY, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and ATTOTNEY interact with these core parties, creating a network of rights, obligations, and potential disputes. The community is characterized by complex legal and financial relationships, with the INSURER holding rights of recovery and the INSURED PERSON entitled to benefits but also subject to reimbursement and cooperation requirements. The presence of arbitration, financial responsibility laws, and material misrepresentation clauses adds layers of regulatory and legal significance.

## Central relationship between INSURER and INSURED PERSON

The INSURER and INSURED PERSON form the core of the insurance community. The INSURER provides financial protection, makes payments on behalf of the insured, and retains rights of recovery and reimbursement. The INSURED PERSON is entitled to benefits such as medical payments and liability coverage, but must also cooperate with the insurer, sign documents, and reimburse payments from liable parties. This relationship is fundamental to the operation of the policy and underlies all other interactions. [Data: Entities (71, 68); Relationships (90, 77, 120, 122, 310, 318, 319, +more)]

## Insurance policy structure and coverage parts

The INSURANCE POLICY is the contract that binds the parties and is divided into three main parts. Part I-Liability to Others covers the insured's liability to third parties, with the insurer's duty to pay contingent on a final determination of the insured's obligation. Part II-Medical Payments Coverage provides for medical expenses due to bodily injury from auto accidents. Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage addresses situations where the other driver is uninsured or underinsured, and may reduce payments under Part I. These parts define the scope of coverage and the conditions under which benefits are paid. [Data: Entities (75, 3, 83, 84, 85); Relationships (106, 158, 18, 19, +more)]

## DEFINITIONS OF LIABLE PARTY AND RECOVERY RIGHTS

The LIABLE PARTY is an entity or individual legally or financially obligated to make payments to an insured person. The insured person may recover from the liable party, and such amounts are held in trust for the insurer. The INSURER holds RECOVERY RIGHTS to the extent of its payments, and the insured must assist in exercising these rights. This dynamic creates a triangular relationship where the insurer seeks reimbursement from the liable party, often requiring the insured's cooperation. [Data: Entities (181, 187, 188); Relationships (310, 319, 320)]

## ROLE OF MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS AND ATTORNEYS

MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS deliver medical services and may sue the insured person if the insurer refuses to pay for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. They may also pursue collection activities. ATTORNEYS represent insured persons in recovering payments from liable parties, with fees shared pro rata by the insurer. These entities introduce potential legal disputes and financial obligations that can escalate the complexity of claims. [Data: Entities (88, 182); Relationships (135, 312)]

## RELATIVE AND RATED RESIDENT AS INSURED PERSONS

A RELATIVE is defined as a family member related by blood, marriage, or adoption, and may qualify as an insured person under the policy, particularly for accidents arising from the ownership, maintenance, or use of an auto. A RATED RESIDENT is included within the definition of an insured person and is covered for auto-related accidents. However, coverage can be affected by factors such as the relative's driver's license status, vehicle ownership or regular use, and intentional acts. These entities expand the scope of who is protected under the policy. [Data: Entities (63, 68); Relationships (77, 110)]

## ARBITRATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

ARBITRATION is a subsection of Part III and is used to determine the legal liability of the operator or owner of an uninsured motor vehicle and the amount of damages sustained by the insured person. Each party selects an arbitrator, and the two arbitrators select a third. The court may appoint the third arbitrator on joint application. This mechanism provides an alternative to litigation for resolving disputes related to uninsured or underinsured motorist claims. [Data: Entities (26, 103, 104); Relationships (34, 167, 166)]

## MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION AND CANCELLATION

MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION is a misrepresentation of a material fact in the procurement, continuation, change, or renewal of the policy, or in the submission of a claim, which constitutes grounds for cancellation after 59 days. This clause protects the insurer from fraud and ensures that the policy is based on accurate information. The insured person's obligation to provide truthful information is thus critical to maintaining coverage. [Data: Entities (173, 184, 70); Relationships (277, 314, 315)]

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS AND OTHER LEGAL REQUIREMENTS

FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS are a subsection of Part I-Liability to Others and mandate that individuals demonstrate the ability to cover damages arising from vehicle accidents, typically through insurance. A policy complies with these laws when properly certified. Additionally, sums paid under workers' compensation or disability benefits laws reduce the limits of liability under Part III. These legal requirements ensure that insured persons meet statutory obligations and that the insurer's liability is coordinated with other sources of compensation. [Data: Entities (21, 99, 100); Relationships (126, 161, 162)]"

We may cancel this policy for any reason if the notice is received by the named insured within the first 59 days of the initial policy period.

## CANCELLATION REFUND

Upon cancellation, you may be entitled to a premium refund. However, our making or offering of a refund is not a condition of cancellation.

If this policy is cancelled, any refund due will be computed on a daily pro rata basis. However, we will retain a cancellation fee if this policy is cancelled at your request or if cancellation is for nonpayment of premium. A cancellation fee will be charged only during the initial policy period.

## NONRENEWAL

If neither we nor one of our affiliates offers to renew or continue this policy , we will mail notice of nonrenewal to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records. A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. Notice will be mailed more than 33 days before the end of the policy period.

## AUTOMATIC TERMINATION

If we or an affiliate offers to renew or continue this policy and you or your representative does not accept, this policy will automatically terminate at the end of the current policy period. Failure to pay the required renewal or continuation premium when due will mean that you have not accepted our offer.

If you obtain other insurance on a covered auto , any similar insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the other insurance.

If a covered auto is sold or transferred to someone other than you or a relative , any insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the sale or transfer.

5|Roadside Assistance Coverage under Part V|"# Roadside Assistance Coverage under Part V

The community centers on Part V of an insurance policy, which provides roadside assistance coverage. Key entities include Covered Disabled Auto, Covered Emergency, Authorized Service Representative, and exclusions for unauthorized service providers and certain facilities. The relationships define the conditions for coverage, the services provided, and the limitations. This community is important for understanding the scope and limitations of roadside assistance insurance, affecting policyholders, insurers, and service providers.

## Part V and Roadside Assistance Coverage

Part V of the insurance policy is dedicated to roadside assistance coverage, which includes towing and labor services for covered disabled autos. This section is a critical component of the policy, providing essential services during emergencies. The coverage is triggered by a covered emergency and is subject to specific conditions and exclusions. [Data: Entities (137, 138); Relationships (211)]

## Definition of Covered Emergency

A covered emergency is defined as a disablement arising from mechanical or electrical breakdown, battery failure, insufficient fluid supply, flat tire, accidental lock-out, or entrapment in snow, mud, water, or sand within 100 feet of a road or highway. This broad definition ensures that various common roadside issues are covered, but it also sets clear boundaries, such as the distance limitation for entrapment. [Data: Entities (146); Relationships (221, 222)]

## Covered Disabled Auto

A covered disabled auto is a covered auto that sustains a covered emergency. This entity is central to the coverage, as it links the vehicle to the emergency event that triggers the roadside assistance services. The coverage is contingent on the auto being covered under the policy and the emergency meeting the defined criteria. [Data: Entities (145); Relationships (221)]

## Authorized Service Representative

An authorized service representative is a service representative authorized by the insurer to provide towing and labor services under Part V. This entity ensures that services are rendered by approved providers, which may affect reimbursement and quality of service. The relationship between the representative and the coverage highlights the importance of using authorized personnel. [Data: Entities (144); Relationships (218)]

## Unauthorized Service Provider Subsection

Part V contains a subsection addressing unauthorized service providers, which likely outlines the consequences of using non-authorized services, such as denial of coverage or reduced reimbursement. This subsection is important for policyholders to understand to avoid unexpected out-of-pocket expenses. [Data: Entities (38); Relationships (51)]

## Exclusions for Service Stations, Garages, and Repair Shops

Labor or repair work performed at a service station, garage, or repair shop is excluded from coverage. These exclusions prevent coverage for routine repairs or maintenance, focusing the coverage on emergency roadside assistance. Policyholders should be aware that work done at these facilities is not covered. [Data: Entities (151, 152, 153); Relationships (235, 236, 237)]

## Part VI and Duties After an Accident or Loss

Part VI of the policy describes duties in case of an accident or loss, including the requirement to protect the covered auto from further loss. This part is related to the roadside assistance coverage as it sets out obligations that may affect claims. The relationship between Part VI and Covered Disabled Auto shows that policyholders must take certain actions to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (148); Relationships (227)]"

Notably, it addresses reimbursement to the insurer contingent on a signed reimbursement agreement and the insurer's pro rata share of attorney fees. Part III-UNINSURED/UNDERINSURED MOTORIST COVERAGE protects policyholders when they are involved in accidents with drivers who have insufficient or no insurance. It includes an insuring agreement, additional definitions, exclusions, limits of liability, other insurance, and arbitration provisions. This coverage is crucial for ensuring that policyholders can recover damages even when the at-fault driver cannot pay. The inclusion of arbitration suggests a mechanism for resolving disputes without litigation. [Data: Entities (5); Relationships (30)]

## Roadside Assistance Coverage and its insuring agreement

Part V-ROADSIDE ASSISTANCE COVERAGE provides services such as towing, jump-starts, and flat tire changes. It includes an insuring agreement that specifies the insurer's promise to pay for these services in exchange for a premium. The part also covers additional definitions, exclusions, unauthorized service provider provisions, and other insurance. This coverage enhances the policy's value by offering practical assistance during vehicle breakdowns or emergencies. [Data: Entities (7, 1); Relationships (49)]

## Duties in Case of an Accident or Loss

Part VI-DUTIES IN CASE OF AN ACCIDENT OR LOSS outlines the policyholder's obligations following an accident or loss, such as promptly notifying the insurer, cooperating in the investigation, and submitting proof of loss. These duties are critical for ensuring timely and accurate claims processing. Failure to comply may result in denial of coverage. This part is contained within the Maine Auto Policy, emphasizing the importance of policyholder responsibilities in the claims process. [Data: Entities (8); Relationships (8)]

Limits of Liability specify the maximum amounts an insurer will pay for covered claims, as detailed on the declarations page. They appear in multiple parts of the policy, including Part I, and are subject to conditions and exclusions. These limits are fundamental in determining the extent of the insurer's financial obligation and are crucial for both policyholders and insurers in managing risk and expectations. The recurring nature of this subsection across different coverage parts ensures consistency in applying monetary caps. [Data: Entities (20); Relationships (129)]"

## PAYMENT OF LOSS

We may, at our option:

- 1 . pay for the loss in money; or
2. repair or replace the damaged or stolen property.

At our expense, we may return any recovered stolen property to you or to the address shown on the declarations page , with payment for any damage resulting from the theft. We may keep all or part of the property at the agreed or appraised value.

We may settle any loss with you or the owner or lienholder of the property .

## LOSS PAYABLE CLAUSE

Payment under this Part IV for a loss to a covered auto will be made according to your interest and the interest of any lienholder shown on the declarations page or designated by you .  At our option, payment may be made to both jointly, or to either separately. However, if the covered auto is not a total loss, we may make payment to you and the repairer of the auto .

The lienholder's interest will not be protected:

- 1 . where fraud, misrepresentation, material omission, or intentional damage resulting in a denial of coverage by us has been committed by or at the direction of you or any person seeking coverage; or
2. where the loss is otherwise not covered under the terms of this policy .

If this policy is cancelled, nonrenewed or voided, the interest of any lienholder under this agreement will also terminate.

## OTHER SOURCES OF RECOVERY

If other sources of recovery also cover the loss, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable

limits. However, any insurance we provide for a non-owned auto , or trailer not shown on the declarations page , will be excess over any other collectible source of recovery including, but not limited to:

- 1 . any coverage provided by the owner of the non-owned auto or trailer ;
2. any other applicable physical damage insurance; and
3. any other source of recovery applicable to the loss.

## APPRAISAL

If we cannot agree with you on the amount of a loss, then we or you may demand an appraisal of the loss. Within 30 days of any demand for an appraisal, each party shall appoint a competent appraiser and shall notify the other party of that appraiser's identity . The appraisers will determine the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, the disagreement will be submitted to a qualified umpire chosen by the appraisers. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days, we or you may request that a judge of a court of record, in the county where you reside, select an umpire. The appraisers and umpire will determine the amount of loss. The amount of loss agreed to by both appraisers, or by one appraiser and the umpire, will be binding. You will pay your appraiser's fees and expenses. We will pay our appraiser's fees and expenses. All other expenses of the appraisal, including payment of the umpire if one is selected, will be shared equally between us and you . 4|Uninsured Motor Vehicle Legal Liability Network|"# Uninsured Motor Vehicle Legal Liability Network

This community comprises entities and relationships that define the legal and insurance framework for uninsured motor vehicles, focusing on key roles such as OWNER and OPERATOR, and the arbitration process involving ARBITRATORS. The central entity, UNINSURED MOTOR VEHICLE, is connected to FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAW, BODILY INJURY LIABILITY BOND, and BODILY INJURY LIABILITY POLICY, which determine its status. The community also includes REPAIRER, who may receive payment jointly with the OWNER in certain situations. The relationships highlight how legal liability is determined and the conditions under which a vehicle is considered uninsured.

## UNINSURED MOTOR VEHICLE as the central entity

UNINSURED MOTOR VEHICLE is the core entity in this community, defined as a land motor vehicle or trailer lacking applicable bodily injury liability coverage, or one whose insurer denies coverage or is insolvent, or whose owner or operator cannot be identified, or that fails to meet minimum liability limits. It has multiple relationships with FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAW, BODILY INJURY LIABILITY BOND, and BODILY INJURY LIABILITY POLICY. Its high degree (10) indicates its importance in connecting various legal and insurance concepts. [Data: Entities (90); Relationships (152, 150, 151)]

## OWNER's role and liability

OWNER refers to a person holding legal ownership over a vehicle, whose permission is required for its use, and may be the owner of an uninsured motor vehicle. The OWNER's legal liability may be determined through arbitration, as indicated by the relationship with ARBITRATORS. Additionally, the OWNER can be the owner of a non-owned auto or trailer, whose insurance coverage may take primary status. The OWNER is also linked to REPAIRER in payment scenarios when the covered auto is not a total loss. [Data: Entities (101); Relationships (170, 217, 175)]

## OPERATOR's responsibilities and scenarios

OPERATOR is defined as an individual involved in the operation of a motor vehicle under specific insurance-related circumstances. The OPERATOR of an uninsured motor vehicle has legal liability determined by arbitration. In another context, the OPERATOR of a covered disabled auto whose intentional or willful act may exclude coverage. This dual definition highlights the operator's role in both uninsured and covered-but-disabled scenarios, emphasizing the operator's direct responsibility and the potential legal or coverage consequences. [Data: Entities (102); Relationships (169)]

## ARBITRATORS' function in determining liability

ARBITRATORS are individuals who make binding decisions regarding legal liability of an uninsured motor vehicle operator or owner and the amount of damages sustained by the insured person. They have a relationship with INSURED PERSON, determining damages, and with OWNER and OPERATOR regarding liability. This role is crucial in resolving disputes arising from uninsured motor vehicle incidents. [Data: Entities (107); Relationships (175, 170, 169)]

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAW's impact on uninsured status

FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAW specifies minimum limits of liability for bodily injury that affect whether a vehicle is uninsured. A vehicle may be uninsured if its liability limit is less than the minimum specified by this law. This entity directly influences the determination of uninsured status, linking statutory requirements to insurance coverage. [Data: Entities (95); Relationships (152)]

## BODILY INJURY LIABILITY BOND and POLICY as coverage determinants

BODILY INJURY LIABILITY BOND and BODILY INJURY LIABILITY POLICY are instruments that may apply to a motor vehicle for bodily injury liability. Their existence, denial, insolvency, or limits affect uninsured motor vehicle status. A vehicle may be uninsured if no bond applies or its limit is insufficient, or if no policy applies, coverage is denied, the insurer is insolvent, or limits are insufficient. These entities are essential in assessing insurance coverage. [Data: Entities (93, 94); Relationships (150, 151)]

## REPAIRER's role in payment scenarios

REPAIRER is a repairer of the auto who may receive payment jointly with the insured when the covered auto is not a total loss. This relationship with OWNER indicates a financial arrangement in insurance claims, highlighting the repairer's involvement in the settlement process. [Data: Entities (143); Relationships (217)]"

1|INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community|"# INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community

The community centers on the relationship between the INSURER and the INSURED PERSON, with the INSURANCE POLICY as the governing contract. The policy is structured into three main coverage parts: Part I-Liability to Others, Part II-Medical Payments Coverage, and Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage. Various entities such as RELATIVE, LIABLE PARTY, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and ATTOTNEY interact with these core parties, creating a network of rights, obligations, and potential disputes. The community is characterized by complex legal and financial relationships, with the INSURER holding rights of recovery and the INSURED PERSON entitled to benefits but also subject to reimbursement and cooperation requirements. The presence of arbitration, financial responsibility laws, and material misrepresentation clauses adds layers of regulatory and legal significance.

## Central relationship between INSURER and INSURED PERSON

The INSURER and INSURED PERSON form the core of the insurance community. The INSURER provides financial protection, makes payments on behalf of the insured, and retains rights of recovery and reimbursement. The INSURED PERSON is entitled to benefits such as medical payments and liability coverage, but must also cooperate with the insurer, sign documents, and reimburse payments from liable parties. This relationship is fundamental to the operation of the policy and underlies all other interactions. [Data: Entities (71, 68); Relationships (90, 77, 120, 122, 310, 318, 319, +more)]

## Insurance policy structure and coverage parts

The INSURANCE POLICY is the contract that binds the parties and is divided into three main parts. Part I-Liability to Others covers the insured's liability to third parties, with the insurer's duty to pay contingent on a final determination of the insured's obligation. Part II-Medical Payments Coverage provides for medical expenses due to bodily injury from auto accidents. Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage addresses situations where the other driver is uninsured or underinsured, and may reduce payments under Part I. These parts define the scope of coverage and the conditions under which benefits are paid. [Data: Entities (75, 3, 83, 84, 85); Relationships (106, 158, 18, 19, +more)]

## DEFINITIONS OF LIABLE PARTY AND RECOVERY RIGHTS

The LIABLE PARTY is an entity or individual legally or financially obligated to make payments to an insured person. The insured person may recover from the liable party, and such amounts are held in trust for the insurer. The INSURER holds RECOVERY RIGHTS to the extent of its payments, and the insured must assist in exercising these rights. This dynamic creates a triangular relationship where the insurer seeks reimbursement from the liable party, often requiring the insured's cooperation. [Data: Entities (181, 187, 188); Relationships (310, 319, 320)]

## ROLE OF MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS AND ATTORNEYS

MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS deliver medical services and may sue the insured person if the insurer refuses to pay for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. They may also pursue collection activities. ATTORNEYS represent insured persons in recovering payments from liable parties, with fees shared pro rata by the insurer. These entities introduce potential legal disputes and financial obligations that can escalate the complexity of claims. [Data: Entities (88, 182); Relationships (135, 312)]

## RELATIVE AND RATED RESIDENT AS INSURED PERSONS

A RELATIVE is defined as a family member related by blood, marriage, or adoption, and may qualify as an insured person under the policy, particularly for accidents arising from the ownership, maintenance, or use of an auto. A RATED RESIDENT is included within the definition of an insured person and is covered for auto-related accidents. However, coverage can be affected by factors such as the relative's driver's license status, vehicle ownership or regular use, and intentional acts. These entities expand the scope of who is protected under the policy. [Data: Entities (63, 68); Relationships (77, 110)]

## ARBITRATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

ARBITRATION is a subsection of Part III and is used to determine the legal liability of the operator or owner of an uninsured motor vehicle and the amount of damages sustained by the insured person. Each party selects an arbitrator, and the two arbitrators select a third. The court may appoint the third arbitrator on joint application. This mechanism provides an alternative to litigation for resolving disputes related to uninsured or underinsured motorist claims. [Data: Entities (26, 103, 104); Relationships (34, 167, 166)]

## MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION AND CANCELLATION

MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION is a misrepresentation of a material fact in the procurement, continuation, change, or renewal of the policy, or in the submission of a claim, which constitutes grounds for cancellation after 59 days. This clause protects the insurer from fraud and ensures that the policy is based on accurate information. The insured person's obligation to provide truthful information is thus critical to maintaining coverage. [Data: Entities (173, 184, 70); Relationships (277, 314, 315)]

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS AND OTHER LEGAL REQUIREMENTS

FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS are a subsection of Part I-Liability to Others and mandate that individuals demonstrate the ability to cover damages arising from vehicle accidents, typically through insurance. A policy complies with these laws when properly certified. Additionally, sums paid under workers' compensation or disability benefits laws reduce the limits of liability under Part III. These legal requirements ensure that insured persons meet statutory obligations and that the insurer's liability is coordinated with other sources of compensation. If the policy is cancelled for nonpayment of premium, we will mail notice of cancellation to you at least 15 days before cancellation takes effect. In all other cases, we will mail notice of cancellation to you at least 25 days before the cancellation takes effect.

We may cancel this policy for any reason if the notice is received by the named insured within the first 59 days of the initial policy period.

After this policy is in effect for more than 59 days, or if this is a renewal or continuation policy , we may cancel only for one or more of the following reasons:

- 1 . nonpayment of premium;

A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. ## CANCELLATION REFUND

Upon cancellation, you may be entitled to a premium refund. However, our making or offering of a refund is not a condition of cancellation.

If this policy is cancelled, any refund due will be computed on a daily pro rata basis. However, we will retain a cancellation fee if this policy is cancelled at your request or if cancellation is for nonpayment of premium. A cancellation fee will be charged only during the initial policy period.

## NONRENEWAL

If neither we nor one of our affiliates offers to renew or continue this policy , we will mail notice of nonrenewal to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records. A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. Notice will be mailed more than 33 days before the end of the policy period.

## AUTOMATIC TERMINATION

If we or an affiliate offers to renew or continue this policy and you or your representative does not accept, this policy will automatically terminate at the end of the current policy period. Failure to pay the required renewal or continuation premium when due will mean that you have not accepted our offer.

If you obtain other insurance on a covered auto , any similar insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the other insurance.

If a covered auto is sold or transferred to someone other than you or a relative , any insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the sale or transfer.

We may not be sued unless there is full compliance with all the terms of this policy .

If we retain salvage, we have no duty to preserve or otherwise retain the salvage for any purpose, including evidence for any civil or criminal proceeding.
