1|INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community|"# INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community

The community centers on the relationship between the INSURER and the INSURED PERSON, with the INSURANCE POLICY as the governing contract. The policy is structured into three main coverage parts: Part I-Liability to Others, Part II-Medical Payments Coverage, and Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage. Various entities such as RELATIVE, LIABLE PARTY, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and ATTOTNEY interact with these core parties, creating a network of rights, obligations, and potential disputes. The community is characterized by complex legal and financial relationships, with the INSURER holding rights of recovery and the INSURED PERSON entitled to benefits but also subject to reimbursement and cooperation requirements. The presence of arbitration, financial responsibility laws, and material misrepresentation clauses adds layers of regulatory and legal significance.

## Central relationship between INSURER and INSURED PERSON

The INSURER and INSURED PERSON form the core of the insurance community. The INSURER provides financial protection, makes payments on behalf of the insured, and retains rights of recovery and reimbursement. The INSURED PERSON is entitled to benefits such as medical payments and liability coverage, but must also cooperate with the insurer, sign documents, and reimburse payments from liable parties. This relationship is fundamental to the operation of the policy and underlies all other interactions. [Data: Entities (71, 68); Relationships (90, 77, 120, 122, 310, 318, 319, +more)]

## Insurance policy structure and coverage parts

The INSURANCE POLICY is the contract that binds the parties and is divided into three main parts. Part I-Liability to Others covers the insured's liability to third parties, with the insurer's duty to pay contingent on a final determination of the insured's obligation. Part II-Medical Payments Coverage provides for medical expenses due to bodily injury from auto accidents. Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage addresses situations where the other driver is uninsured or underinsured, and may reduce payments under Part I. These parts define the scope of coverage and the conditions under which benefits are paid. [Data: Entities (75, 3, 83, 84, 85); Relationships (106, 158, 18, 19, +more)]

## DEFINITIONS OF LIABLE PARTY AND RECOVERY RIGHTS

The LIABLE PARTY is an entity or individual legally or financially obligated to make payments to an insured person. The insured person may recover from the liable party, and such amounts are held in trust for the insurer. The INSURER holds RECOVERY RIGHTS to the extent of its payments, and the insured must assist in exercising these rights. This dynamic creates a triangular relationship where the insurer seeks reimbursement from the liable party, often requiring the insured's cooperation. [Data: Entities (181, 187, 188); Relationships (310, 319, 320)]

## ROLE OF MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS AND ATTORNEYS

MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS deliver medical services and may sue the insured person if the insurer refuses to pay for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. They may also pursue collection activities. ATTORNEYS represent insured persons in recovering payments from liable parties, with fees shared pro rata by the insurer. These entities introduce potential legal disputes and financial obligations that can escalate the complexity of claims. [Data: Entities (88, 182); Relationships (135, 312)]

## RELATIVE AND RATED RESIDENT AS INSURED PERSONS

A RELATIVE is defined as a family member related by blood, marriage, or adoption, and may qualify as an insured person under the policy, particularly for accidents arising from the ownership, maintenance, or use of an auto. A RATED RESIDENT is included within the definition of an insured person and is covered for auto-related accidents. However, coverage can be affected by factors such as the relative's driver's license status, vehicle ownership or regular use, and intentional acts. These entities expand the scope of who is protected under the policy. [Data: Entities (63, 68); Relationships (77, 110)]

## ARBITRATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

ARBITRATION is a subsection of Part III and is used to determine the legal liability of the operator or owner of an uninsured motor vehicle and the amount of damages sustained by the insured person. Each party selects an arbitrator, and the two arbitrators select a third. The court may appoint the third arbitrator on joint application. This mechanism provides an alternative to litigation for resolving disputes related to uninsured or underinsured motorist claims. [Data: Entities (26, 103, 104); Relationships (34, 167, 166)]

## MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION AND CANCELLATION

MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION is a misrepresentation of a material fact in the procurement, continuation, change, or renewal of the policy, or in the submission of a claim, which constitutes grounds for cancellation after 59 days. This clause protects the insurer from fraud and ensures that the policy is based on accurate information. The insured person's obligation to provide truthful information is thus critical to maintaining coverage. [Data: Entities (173, 184, 70); Relationships (277, 314, 315)]

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS AND OTHER LEGAL REQUIREMENTS

FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS are a subsection of Part I-Liability to Others and mandate that individuals demonstrate the ability to cover damages arising from vehicle accidents, typically through insurance. A policy complies with these laws when properly certified. Additionally, sums paid under workers' compensation or disability benefits laws reduce the limits of liability under Part III. These legal requirements ensure that insured persons meet statutory obligations and that the insurer's liability is coordinated with other sources of compensation. [Data: Entities (21, 99, 100); Relationships (126, 161, 162)]"

0|Auto Insurance Policy Community: Covered Auto and Exclusions|"# Auto Insurance Policy Community: Covered Auto and Exclusions

This community represents an auto insurance policy framework centered on the definition of a 'covered auto' and its relationships with various policy terms, exclusions, and conditions. Key entities include covered auto, declarations page, auto, trailer, additional auto, replacement auto, out-of-state coverage, and exclusions such as racing, stunting, and ride-sharing activity. The community illustrates how coverage is determined, what vehicles qualify, and the circumstances under which coverage may be excluded or extended.

## Central role of covered auto

The entity 'COVERED AUTO' serves as the central node in this community, connecting to multiple other entities that define its scope and limitations. A covered auto is defined as any auto or trailer shown on the declarations page, any additional auto, any replacement auto, or a trailer owned by the insured, and it is subject to various exclusions and limits. This definition is foundational for determining which vehicles are insured under the policy. The high degree of the covered auto entity (28) and its numerous relationships (e.g., with AUTO, TRAILER, and various exclusions) highlight its importance in the policy structure. [Data: Entities (58, 12, 14, 66, 11, 64); Relationships (70, 81, 72, 73, 200, +more)]

## Declarations page as the source of coverage details

The 'DECLARATIONS PAGE' is a critical document that summarizes essential policy details, including coverages, limits of liability, and the autos insured. It shows the covered autos and may also display the combined single limit (CSL) and other policy-related information. The declarations page is linked to the covered auto entity, indicating that it is the primary reference for identifying which vehicles are covered. Additionally, it includes sections such as the Drivers and Household Residents section, which lists rated residents and other drivers. [Data: Entities (14, 58, 106, 72, 62); Relationships (81, 172, 102, 101)]

## Exclusions that limit coverage

Several entities represent activities or circumstances for which coverage is excluded under the policy. These include racing, stunting, demolition contests, racetrack or racecourse use, nuclear energy liability insurance contracts, and mechanical parts breakdown. Each of these exclusions is directly linked to the covered auto entity, indicating that coverage does not apply when a covered auto is used in these contexts. For instance, coverage is excluded for a vehicle during racing, stunting, or a demolition contest, as well as for driving activities on a racetrack. These exclusions are important for understanding the boundaries of coverage. [Data: Entities (123, 124, 125, 126, 127, 128); Relationships (201, 202, 203, 204, 206, 208)]

## Ride-sharing and carpool distinctions

The community includes entities related to ride-sharing activity and shared-expense car pools, which have distinct treatment under the policy. 'RIDE-SHARING ACTIVITY' is defined as the use of any vehicle to provide transportation in connection with a transportation network company, and it is specifically excluded from coverage. In contrast, 'SHARED-EXPENSE CAR POOLS' are excluded from the ride-sharing exclusion, meaning coverage may still apply to traditional carpool arrangements. This distinction is crucial for policyholders who participate in carpooling versus those who drive for ride-sharing companies. [Data: Entities (65, 122, 67); Relationships (200, 75)]

## Additional and replacement autos

The policy provides definitions for 'ADDITIONAL AUTO' and 'REPLACEMENT AUTO', which are types of covered autos under certain conditions. An additional auto is one the policyholder becomes the owner of during the policy period that does not permanently replace an auto shown on the declarations page, subject to notification within 30 days and payment of additional premium. A replacement auto permanently replaces an auto shown on the declarations page. Both are linked to the covered auto entity, indicating that they qualify for coverage if the policy conditions are met. [Data: Entities (11, 64, 58, 55); Relationships (17, 73, 10, 70)]

## Out-of-state coverage extension

The 'OUT-OF-STATE COVERAGE' provision extends the policy's liability limits to comply with higher requirements in other states, territories, or provinces when an accident occurs outside the state where the covered auto is principally garaged. This coverage applies within the United States of America and Canada. The provision ensures that policyholders retain liability protection sufficient to satisfy mandatory financial responsibility laws in the jurisdiction where the accident occurs. This entity is linked to the covered auto and to the geographical entities (USA and Canada), highlighting its role in addressing varying legal requirements. [Data: Entities (23, 58, 147, 86); Relationships (127, 131, 132)]

## Rated residents and household drivers

The 'RATED RESIDENT' entity represents a non-relative household member listed and rated on the policy, whose licensing status, vehicle ownership, and vehicle use carry specific coverage implications. Rated residents are listed in the Drivers and Household Residents section of the declarations page and are treated similarly to relatives for coverage purposes under Part I, though they may be subject to different rates or coverage terms. Their loss of driving privileges can be a reason for policy cancellation. This entity is linked to the declarations page and the drivers section, emphasizing the importance of accurately listing household members. [Data: Entities (62, 72, 14); Relationships (101, 102)]

## Policy period and territory

The 'POLICY PERIOD' entity defines the timeframe during which the insurance policy is in effect, as shown on the declarations page. It is the period within which cancellation or license revocation is assessed. The policy applies only to accidents and losses occurring during this period, as stated in Part VII. The territory of coverage includes the United States of America and Canada, as indicated by the out-of-state coverage provision. These temporal and geographical limitations are essential for understanding when and where coverage applies. [Data: Entities (150, 149, 147, 86); Relationships (228, 280, 131, 132)]

## Premium and insuring agreement

The 'PREMIUM' entity represents the payment made by the policyholder in return for the insurer's agreement to insure. It is linked to the insuring agreement, indicating that coverage is contingent upon payment. Additionally, an additional premium may be due for an additional auto, as specified in the relationship between additional auto and premium. The premium is a fundamental aspect of the insurance contract, as it establishes the consideration for coverage. [Data: Entities (55, 11); Relationships (16, 17)]

## Auto definition and weight restrictions

The 'AUTO' entity is defined as a land motor vehicle of the private passenger or pickup body type, including cargo vans, designed for operation principally upon public roads, with at least four wheels and a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of 12,000 pounds or less. This definition is critical for determining which vehicles qualify as autos under the policy, and it is linked to the covered auto entity and the gross vehicle weight rating entity. The weight restriction ensures that larger vehicles are excluded from this definition. [Data: Entities (12, 76, 58, 66); Relationships (70, 108)]"

1|INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community|"# INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community

The community centers on the relationship between the INSURER and the INSURED PERSON, with the INSURANCE POLICY as the governing contract. The policy is structured into three main coverage parts: Part I-Liability to Others, Part II-Medical Payments Coverage, and Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage. Various entities such as RELATIVE, LIABLE PARTY, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and ATTOTNEY interact with these core parties, creating a network of rights, obligations, and potential disputes. The community is characterized by complex legal and financial relationships, with the INSURER holding rights of recovery and the INSURED PERSON entitled to benefits but also subject to reimbursement and cooperation requirements. The presence of arbitration, financial responsibility laws, and material misrepresentation clauses adds layers of regulatory and legal significance.

## Central relationship between INSURER and INSURED PERSON

The INSURER and INSURED PERSON form the core of the insurance community. The INSURER provides financial protection, makes payments on behalf of the insured, and retains rights of recovery and reimbursement. The INSURED PERSON is entitled to benefits such as medical payments and liability coverage, but must also cooperate with the insurer, sign documents, and reimburse payments from liable parties. This relationship is fundamental to the operation of the policy and underlies all other interactions. [Data: Entities (71, 68); Relationships (90, 77, 120, 122, 310, 318, 319, +more)]

## Insurance policy structure and coverage parts

The INSURANCE POLICY is the contract that binds the parties and is divided into three main parts. Part I-Liability to Others covers the insured's liability to third parties, with the insurer's duty to pay contingent on a final determination of the insured's obligation. Part II-Medical Payments Coverage provides for medical expenses due to bodily injury from auto accidents. Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage addresses situations where the other driver is uninsured or underinsured, and may reduce payments under Part I. These parts define the scope of coverage and the conditions under which benefits are paid. [Data: Entities (75, 3, 83, 84, 85); Relationships (106, 158, 18, 19, +more)]

## DEFINITIONS OF LIABLE PARTY AND RECOVERY RIGHTS

The LIABLE PARTY is an entity or individual legally or financially obligated to make payments to an insured person. The insured person may recover from the liable party, and such amounts are held in trust for the insurer. The INSURER holds RECOVERY RIGHTS to the extent of its payments, and the insured must assist in exercising these rights. This dynamic creates a triangular relationship where the insurer seeks reimbursement from the liable party, often requiring the insured's cooperation. [Data: Entities (181, 187, 188); Relationships (310, 319, 320)]

## ROLE OF MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS AND ATTORNEYS

MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS deliver medical services and may sue the insured person if the insurer refuses to pay for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. They may also pursue collection activities. ATTORNEYS represent insured persons in recovering payments from liable parties, with fees shared pro rata by the insurer. These entities introduce potential legal disputes and financial obligations that can escalate the complexity of claims. [Data: Entities (88, 182); Relationships (135, 312)]

## RELATIVE AND RATED RESIDENT AS INSURED PERSONS

A RELATIVE is defined as a family member related by blood, marriage, or adoption, and may qualify as an insured person under the policy, particularly for accidents arising from the ownership, maintenance, or use of an auto. A RATED RESIDENT is included within the definition of an insured person and is covered for auto-related accidents. However, coverage can be affected by factors such as the relative's driver's license status, vehicle ownership or regular use, and intentional acts. These entities expand the scope of who is protected under the policy. [Data: Entities (63, 68); Relationships (77, 110)]

## ARBITRATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

ARBITRATION is a subsection of Part III and is used to determine the legal liability of the operator or owner of an uninsured motor vehicle and the amount of damages sustained by the insured person. Each party selects an arbitrator, and the two arbitrators select a third. The court may appoint the third arbitrator on joint application. This mechanism provides an alternative to litigation for resolving disputes related to uninsured or underinsured motorist claims. [Data: Entities (26, 103, 104); Relationships (34, 167, 166)]

## MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION AND CANCELLATION

MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION is a misrepresentation of a material fact in the procurement, continuation, change, or renewal of the policy, or in the submission of a claim, which constitutes grounds for cancellation after 59 days. This clause protects the insurer from fraud and ensures that the policy is based on accurate information. The insured person's obligation to provide truthful information is thus critical to maintaining coverage. [Data: Entities (173, 184, 70); Relationships (277, 314, 315)]

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS AND OTHER LEGAL REQUIREMENTS

FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS are a subsection of Part I-Liability to Others and mandate that individuals demonstrate the ability to cover damages arising from vehicle accidents, typically through insurance. A policy complies with these laws when properly certified. Additionally, sums paid under workers' compensation or disability benefits laws reduce the limits of liability under Part III. These legal requirements ensure that insured persons meet statutory obligations and that the insurer's liability is coordinated with other sources of compensation. [Data: Entities (21, 99, 100); Relationships (126, 161, 162)]"

- 1 . a financial responsibility or similar law requiring limits of liability for bodily injury or property damage higher than the limits shown on the declarations page , this policy will provide the higher limits; or

2. a compulsory insurance or similar law requiring a non-resident to maintain insurance whenever the non-resident uses an auto in that state, province, territory or possession, this policy will provide the greater of:
- a. the required minimum amounts and types of coverage; or
- b. the limits of liability under this policy .

## INSURING AGREEMENT

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay the reasonable expenses incurred for necessary medical services received within three years from the date of a motor vehicle accident because of bodily injury :

- 1 . sustained by an insured person ; and
2. caused by that motor vehicle accident.

## We , or someone on our behalf, will determine:

- 1 . whether the expenses for medical services are reasonable; and
2. whether the medical services are necessary.

## When used in this Part II:

## UNREASONABLE OR UNNECESSARY MEDICAL EXPENSES

If an insured person incurs expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them.

If the medical service provider sues the insured person because we refuse to pay expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we will pay any resulting defense costs, and any resulting judgment against the insured person , subject to the limit of liability for this coverage. We will choose the counsel. We will also pay reasonable expenses, including loss of earnings up to $200 per day, incurred at our request.

The insured person may not sue us for expenses for medical services we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary unless the insured person paid the entire disputed amount to the medical service provider or the medical service provider has initiated collection activity against the insured person for the unreasonable or unnecessary expenses.

## OTHER INSURANCE

If there is other applicable auto medical payments insurance, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable limits. However, any insurance we provide for an insured person occupying a vehicle or trailer, other than a covered auto , will be excess over any other auto insurance providing payments for medical services .

## INSURING AGREEMENT

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for damages that an insured person is legally entitled to recover from the owner or operator of an uninsured motor vehicle because of bodily injury :

- 1 . sustained by an insured person ;
2. caused by an accident; and
3. arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use of an uninsured motor vehicle .

We will pay under this Part III only after the limits of liability under all applicable bodily injury liability bonds and policies have been exhausted by payment of judgments or settlements.

Any judgment or settlement for damages against an owner or operator of an uninsured motor vehicle that arises out of a lawsuit brought without our written consent is not binding on us .

7|Maine Auto Policy and Its Coverage Structure|"# Maine Auto Policy and Its Coverage Structure

The community is centered on the Maine Auto Policy, a comprehensive auto insurance policy issued in Maine. It comprises multiple coverage parts: Part II (Medical Payments), Part III (Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist), Part IV (Damage to a Vehicle), Part V (Roadside Assistance), and Part VI (Duties in Case of Accident or Loss). Part IV is the most detailed, containing numerous insuring agreements for collision, comprehensive, custom parts, rental reimbursement, loan/lease payoff, and pet injury, along with payment of loss, no benefit to bailee, loss payable clause, and other sources of recovery. Common subsections such as Exclusions, Other Insurance, Additional Definitions, and Limits of Liability appear across multiple parts. The policy is governed by a Policy Contract that includes the insurance application and endorsements.

## Centrality of Part IV-Damage to a Vehicle

Part IV-Damage to a Vehicle is the most connected entity in the community, with a degree of 17, indicating its central role in the policy structure. It encompasses various coverage types, including collision, comprehensive, custom parts, rental reimbursement, loan/lease payoff, and pet injury, each addressed in separate insuring agreements. This part also includes subsections on payment of loss, no benefit to bailee, loss payable clause, and other sources of recovery, making it a comprehensive section for vehicle damage claims. Subsections such as Exclusions, Other Insurance, Additional Definitions, and Limits of Liability appear in multiple parts of the policy, reflecting their importance in defining the scope and limitations of coverage. Exclusions specify what is not covered, while Other Insurance addresses coordination with other policies. Additional Definitions provide clarity on terms, and Limits of Liability set maximum payment amounts. These recurring subsections ensure consistency and comprehensiveness across different coverage parts, helping to avoid ambiguity and manage risk. [Data: Entities (19, 22, 24, 20); Relationships (20, 23, 25, 28, 30, 49)]

The Policy Contract forms the legal foundation of the insurance agreement, incorporating the insurance application, declarations page, and endorsements. The Insuring Agreement within the policy contract specifies that the policy consists of these documents, establishing the terms of coverage. This structure ensures that the policyholder and insurer have a clear understanding of their rights and obligations, with endorsements allowing for modifications to the standard policy. The contract's components are essential for legal enforcement and claims resolution. [Data: Entities (16, 13, 15, 1); Relationships (12, 13, 15)]

## Geographic applicability and legal jurisdiction

The Maine Auto Policy is specifically applicable in the state of Maine, as indicated by its relationship with the entity 'MAINE'. This geographic limitation means that coverage terms and conditions are subject to Maine state laws and regulations, which may differ from other states. Policyholders and insurers must adhere to Maine-specific requirements, including mandatory coverages and claim handling procedures. This localization impacts the policy's interpretation and enforcement. [Data: Entities (0, 10); Relationships (0)]

This part also includes a subsection on unreasonable or unnecessary medical expenses, highlighting the insurer's scrutiny of claims. The comprehensive nature of this coverage underscores its importance in protecting policyholders from medical costs. [Data: Entities (4, 25); Relationships (25, 28)]

## Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage and its scope

Part III-UNINSURED/UNDERINSURED MOTORIST COVERAGE protects policyholders when they are involved in accidents with drivers who have insufficient or no insurance. It includes an insuring agreement, additional definitions, exclusions, limits of liability, other insurance, and arbitration provisions. This coverage is crucial for ensuring that policyholders can recover damages even when the at-fault driver cannot pay. The inclusion of arbitration suggests a mechanism for resolving disputes without litigation. [Data: Entities (5); Relationships (30)]

Part V-ROADSIDE ASSISTANCE COVERAGE provides services such as towing, jump-starts, and flat tire changes. It includes an insuring agreement that specifies the insurer's promise to pay for these services in exchange for a premium. This coverage enhances the policy's value by offering practical assistance during vehicle breakdowns or emergencies. [Data: Entities (7, 1); Relationships (49)]

Part VI-DUTIES IN CASE OF AN ACCIDENT OR LOSS outlines the policyholder's obligations following an accident or loss, such as promptly notifying the insurer, cooperating in the investigation, and submitting proof of loss. These duties are critical for ensuring timely and accurate claims processing. Failure to comply may result in denial of coverage. This part is contained within the Maine Auto Policy, emphasizing the importance of policyholder responsibilities in the claims process. [Data: Entities (8); Relationships (8)]

Limits of Liability specify the maximum amounts an insurer will pay for covered claims, as detailed on the declarations page. These limits are fundamental in determining the extent of the insurer's financial obligation and are crucial for both policyholders and insurers in managing risk and expectations. 1|INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community|"# INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community

The community centers on the relationship between the INSURER and the INSURED PERSON, with the INSURANCE POLICY as the governing contract. The policy is structured into three main coverage parts: Part I-Liability to Others, Part II-Medical Payments Coverage, and Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage. Various entities such as RELATIVE, LIABLE PARTY, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and ATTOTNEY interact with these core parties, creating a network of rights, obligations, and potential disputes. The community is characterized by complex legal and financial relationships, with the INSURER holding rights of recovery and the INSURED PERSON entitled to benefits but also subject to reimbursement and cooperation requirements. The presence of arbitration, financial responsibility laws, and material misrepresentation clauses adds layers of regulatory and legal significance.

## Central relationship between INSURER and INSURED PERSON

The INSURER and INSURED PERSON form the core of the insurance community. The INSURER provides financial protection, makes payments on behalf of the insured, and retains rights of recovery and reimbursement. The INSURED PERSON is entitled to benefits such as medical payments and liability coverage, but must also cooperate with the insurer, sign documents, and reimburse payments from liable parties. This relationship is fundamental to the operation of the policy and underlies all other interactions. [Data: Entities (71, 68); Relationships (90, 77, 120, 122, 310, 318, 319, +more)]

## Insurance policy structure and coverage parts

The INSURANCE POLICY is the contract that binds the parties and is divided into three main parts. Part I-Liability to Others covers the insured's liability to third parties, with the insurer's duty to pay contingent on a final determination of the insured's obligation. Part II-Medical Payments Coverage provides for medical expenses due to bodily injury from auto accidents. Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage addresses situations where the other driver is uninsured or underinsured, and may reduce payments under Part I. These parts define the scope of coverage and the conditions under which benefits are paid. [Data: Entities (75, 3, 83, 84, 85); Relationships (106, 158, 18, 19, +more)]

## DEFINITIONS OF LIABLE PARTY AND RECOVERY RIGHTS

The LIABLE PARTY is an entity or individual legally or financially obligated to make payments to an insured person. The insured person may recover from the liable party, and such amounts are held in trust for the insurer. The INSURER holds RECOVERY RIGHTS to the extent of its payments, and the insured must assist in exercising these rights. This dynamic creates a triangular relationship where the insurer seeks reimbursement from the liable party, often requiring the insured's cooperation. [Data: Entities (181, 187, 188); Relationships (310, 319, 320)]

## ROLE OF MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS AND ATTORNEYS

MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS deliver medical services and may sue the insured person if the insurer refuses to pay for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. They may also pursue collection activities. ATTORNEYS represent insured persons in recovering payments from liable parties, with fees shared pro rata by the insurer. These entities introduce potential legal disputes and financial obligations that can escalate the complexity of claims. [Data: Entities (88, 182); Relationships (135, 312)]

## RELATIVE AND RATED RESIDENT AS INSURED PERSONS

A RELATIVE is defined as a family member related by blood, marriage, or adoption, and may qualify as an insured person under the policy, particularly for accidents arising from the ownership, maintenance, or use of an auto. A RATED RESIDENT is included within the definition of an insured person and is covered for auto-related accidents. However, coverage can be affected by factors such as the relative's driver's license status, vehicle ownership or regular use, and intentional acts. These entities expand the scope of who is protected under the policy. [Data: Entities (63, 68); Relationships (77, 110)]

## ARBITRATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

ARBITRATION is a subsection of Part III and is used to determine the legal liability of the operator or owner of an uninsured motor vehicle and the amount of damages sustained by the insured person. Each party selects an arbitrator, and the two arbitrators select a third. The court may appoint the third arbitrator on joint application. This mechanism provides an alternative to litigation for resolving disputes related to uninsured or underinsured motorist claims. [Data: Entities (26, 103, 104); Relationships (34, 167, 166)]

## MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION AND CANCELLATION

MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION is a misrepresentation of a material fact in the procurement, continuation, change, or renewal of the policy, or in the submission of a claim, which constitutes grounds for cancellation after 59 days. This clause protects the insurer from fraud and ensures that the policy is based on accurate information. The insured person's obligation to provide truthful information is thus critical to maintaining coverage. [Data: Entities (173, 184, 70); Relationships (277, 314, 315)]

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS AND OTHER LEGAL REQUIREMENTS

FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS are a subsection of Part I-Liability to Others and mandate that individuals demonstrate the ability to cover damages arising from vehicle accidents, typically through insurance. A policy complies with these laws when properly certified. Additionally, sums paid under workers' compensation or disability benefits laws reduce the limits of liability under Part III. These legal requirements ensure that insured persons meet statutory obligations and that the insurer's liability is coordinated with other sources of compensation. [Data: Entities (21, 99, 100); Relationships (126, 161, 162)]"

## LIMITS OF LIABILITY

The limit of liability shown on the declarations page for liability coverage is the most we will pay regardless of the number of:

- 1 . claims made;
2. covered autos ;
3. insured persons ;
4. lawsuits brought;
5. vehicles involved in the accident; or
6. premiums paid.

## If your declarations page shows a split limit:

- 1 . the amount shown for 'each person' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury to one person resulting from any one accident;
2. subject to the 'each person' limit, the amount shown for 'each accident' is the most we will pay for all damages due to bodily injury sustained by two or more persons in any one accident; and
3. the amount shown for 'property damage' is the most we will pay for the total of all property damage resulting from any one accident.

The 'each person' limit of liability applies to the total of all claims made for bodily injury to a person and all claims of others derived from such bodily injury , including, but not

limited to, emotional injury or mental anguish resulting from the bodily injury of another or from witnessing the bodily injury to another, loss of society , loss of companionship, loss of services, loss of consortium, and wrongful death.

If  the declarations  page shows  that  'combined  single  limit'  or  'CSL '  applies,  the amount shown is the most we will pay for the total of all damages resulting from any one accident. However, without changing this limit of liability , we will comply with any law that requires us to provide any separate limits.

No one is entitled to duplicate payments for the same elements of damages.

Any payment to a person under this Part I will be reduced by any payment to that person under Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage.

We will not pay under this Part I any expenses paid or payable under Part II-Medical Payments Coverage.

If multiple auto policies issued by us are in effect for you , we will pay no more than the highest limit of liability for this coverage available under any one policy .

An auto and attached trailer are considered one auto .  Therefore, the limits of liability will not be increased for an accident involving an auto that has an attached trailer .

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS

When we certify this policy as proof of financial responsibility , this policy will comply with the law to the extent required. The insured person must reimburse us if we make a payment that we would not have made if this policy was not certified as proof of financial responsibility .

## OTHER INSURANCE

If there is any other applicable liability insurance or bond, any liability insurance we provide will be excess over any other applicable liability insurance or bond. If more than one liability insurance policy or bond applies on an excess basis, we will pay only our share of the damages. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable limits.

## OUT-OF-STATE COVERAGE

If an accident to which this Part I applies occurs in any state, territory or possession of the United States of America or any province or territory of Canada, other than the one in which a covered auto is principally garaged, and the state, province, territory or possession has:

- 1 . a financial responsibility or similar law requiring limits of liability for bodily injury or property damage higher than the limits shown on the declarations page , this policy will provide the higher limits; or

- a. the required minimum amounts and types of coverage; or
- b. the limits of liability under this policy .

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay the reasonable expenses incurred for necessary medical services received within three years from the date of a motor vehicle accident because of bodily injury :

5|Roadside Assistance Coverage under Part V|"# Roadside Assistance Coverage under Part V

The community centers on Part V of an insurance policy, which provides roadside assistance coverage. Key entities include Covered Disabled Auto, Covered Emergency, Authorized Service Representative, and exclusions for unauthorized service providers and certain facilities. The relationships define the conditions for coverage, the services provided, and the limitations. This community is important for understanding the scope and limitations of roadside assistance insurance, affecting policyholders, insurers, and service providers.

## Part V and Roadside Assistance Coverage

Part V of the insurance policy is dedicated to roadside assistance coverage, which includes towing and labor services for covered disabled autos. This section is a critical component of the policy, providing essential services during emergencies. The coverage is triggered by a covered emergency and is subject to specific conditions and exclusions. [Data: Entities (137, 138); Relationships (211)]

## Definition of Covered Emergency

A covered emergency is defined as a disablement arising from mechanical or electrical breakdown, battery failure, insufficient fluid supply, flat tire, accidental lock-out, or entrapment in snow, mud, water, or sand within 100 feet of a road or highway. This broad definition ensures that various common roadside issues are covered, but it also sets clear boundaries, such as the distance limitation for entrapment. [Data: Entities (146); Relationships (221, 222)]

## Covered Disabled Auto

A covered disabled auto is a covered auto that sustains a covered emergency. This entity is central to the coverage, as it links the vehicle to the emergency event that triggers the roadside assistance services. The coverage is contingent on the auto being covered under the policy and the emergency meeting the defined criteria. [Data: Entities (145); Relationships (221)]

## Authorized Service Representative

An authorized service representative is a service representative authorized by the insurer to provide towing and labor services under Part V. This entity ensures that services are rendered by approved providers, which may affect reimbursement and quality of service. The relationship between the representative and the coverage highlights the importance of using authorized personnel. [Data: Entities (144); Relationships (218)]

## Unauthorized Service Provider Subsection

Part V contains a subsection addressing unauthorized service providers, which likely outlines the consequences of using non-authorized services, such as denial of coverage or reduced reimbursement. This subsection is important for policyholders to understand to avoid unexpected out-of-pocket expenses. [Data: Entities (38); Relationships (51)]

## Exclusions for Service Stations, Garages, and Repair Shops

Labor or repair work performed at a service station, garage, or repair shop is excluded from coverage. These exclusions prevent coverage for routine repairs or maintenance, focusing the coverage on emergency roadside assistance. Policyholders should be aware that work done at these facilities is not covered. [Data: Entities (151, 152, 153); Relationships (235, 236, 237)]

## Part VI and Duties After an Accident or Loss

Part VI of the policy describes duties in case of an accident or loss, including the requirement to protect the covered auto from further loss. This part is related to the roadside assistance coverage as it sets out obligations that may affect claims. The relationship between Part VI and Covered Disabled Auto shows that policyholders must take certain actions to maintain coverage. [Data: Entities (148); Relationships (227)]"

6|Named Insured and Auto Insurance Policy Provisions|"# Named Insured and Auto Insurance Policy Provisions

The community centers on the Named Insured and the auto insurance policy structure, including coverage types such as Collision, Comprehensive, Loan or Lease, and Pet Injury Coverage. Key entities include the Named Insured, Spouse, Auto Business, and various policy parts and coverages. Relationships reveal the conditions and dependencies between coverages, the role of the Named Insured, and exclusions, forming a complex network of insurance definitions and provisions.

## The Named Insured as the central policyholder

The Named Insured is the primary entity in this community, defined as the person specifically identified on the declarations page of an insurance policy. This individual holds the authority to cancel or modify the policy, and such actions bind all other covered persons. The Named Insured is also the recipient of cancellation and nonrenewal notices. The relationship between the Named Insured and the Declarations Page is fundamental, as the latter serves as the authoritative document identifying the former. Additionally, the spouse of the Named Insured may be included as an insured if residing in the same household, extending coverage. The centrality of the Named Insured underscores the importance of clearly identifying and notifying this party in insurance contracts. [Data: Entities (73, 74); Relationships (103, 105)]

## Dependencies among auto insurance coverages

The community features several interlocking coverages: Collision Coverage, Comprehensive Coverage, Loan or Lease Coverage, and Pet Injury Coverage. Pet Injury Coverage requires the insured to have purchased Collision coverage for at least one covered auto, and it also requires the pet to be injured during a loss covered under Collision or Comprehensive coverage. Loan/Lease Coverage applies only if the insured has purchased both Comprehensive and Collision coverage. These dependencies illustrate the layered nature of auto insurance, where broader coverages enable additional protections. Understanding these relationships is crucial for policyholders to ensure adequate coverage. [Data: Entities (114, 113, 115, 116); Relationships (186, 187, 188)]

## Transfer of Interest and General Provisions

The Transfer of Interest is a policy event and a subsection of Part VII–General Provisions, governing the assignment of rights and duties under a policy to another person. This mechanism allows for the movement of rights and obligations, and its placement within General Provisions indicates its procedural importance. Part VII contains this subsection, establishing the rules for effecting transfers. This entity is part of the broader policy structure, ensuring that changes in policy ownership are properly managed. [Data: Entities (44); Relationships (58)]

## Auto Business and its role in exclusions

An Auto Business is defined as a commercial entity engaged in selling, leasing, repairing, parking, storing, servicing, delivering, or testing vehicles. This definition is often referenced in insurance policies to delineate exclusions, as activities of auto businesses may be excluded from certain coverages. The relationship between Auto Business and Auto highlights the scope of operations covered. Auto dealerships, a specific type of auto business, may install custom parts as part of the original sale of a new auto, and such parts are excluded from Custom Parts or Equipment coverage. This illustrates how business activities interact with policy exclusions. [Data: Entities (56, 118, 129); Relationships (84, 209)]

## Conditions for Pet Injury Coverage

Pet Injury Coverage provides up to $1,000 for veterinary fees or a $1,000 death benefit if a pet (dog or cat) is injured or dies in a covered auto during a covered loss. This coverage is contingent on the insured having purchased Collision coverage and requires the loss to be covered under Collision or Comprehensive coverage. Additionally, if a pet is inside a covered auto at the time of theft and not recovered, a death benefit may be provided. These conditions highlight the specific circumstances under which pet injury protection applies, emphasizing the need for appropriate primary coverages. [Data: Entities (115, 121); Relationships (186, 187, 198)]

## Loan or Lease Coverage and its reductions

Loan or Lease Coverage pays under a written loan or lease agreement for a covered auto at the time of total loss, but the payment is reduced by various charges. Specifically, charges for credit insurance and extended warranties reduce the loan or lease coverage payment. This coverage requires the insured to have purchased both Comprehensive and Collision coverage. The reductions reflect typical deductions in total loss settlements, ensuring that the coverage aligns with actual financial obligations. [Data: Entities (116, 119, 120); Relationships (188, 196, 197)]

## Exclusions and limitations in Part IV coverage

Part IV of the insurance policy covers physical damage to vehicles, including payment of loss and lienholder interests. However, coverage under Part IV will not benefit any carrier or other bailee for hire. Additionally, coverage is excluded for destruction or confiscation by governmental or civil authorities due to illegal activities. These exclusions and limitations define the boundaries of physical damage coverage, ensuring that certain entities and events are not covered. [Data: Entities (136, 139, 117); Relationships (223, 193)]"

## PART IV-DAMAGE TO A VEHICLE

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COLLISION COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , resulting from collision .

In addition, we will pay the reasonable cost to replace any child safety seat damaged in an accident to which this coverage applies.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to a:

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;
5. missiles or falling objects;
6. riot or civil commotion;
- 7 . theft or larceny;
8. windstorm, hail, water or flood; or
9. breakage of glass not caused by collision .

## In addition, we will pay for:

- 1 . reasonable transportation expenses incurred by you if a covered auto is stolen; and
2. loss of use damages that you are legally liable to pay if a non-owned auto is stolen. A combined maximum of $900, not exceeding $30 per day, will apply to these additional benefits. The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;
2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;
3. when the auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

5. if the loss is theft of a rented non-owned auto , 30 days after loss of use begins on the loss.

We must receive written proof of transportation expenses and loss of use damages.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-ADDITIONAL CUSTOM PARTS OR EQUIPMENT COVERAGE

We will pay for sudden, direct and accidental loss to custom parts or equipment on a covered auto for which this coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages. This coverage applies in addition to any coverage automatically provided for custom parts or equipment under Comprehensive Coverage or Collision Coverage.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-RENTAL REIMBURSEMENT COVERAGE

We will reimburse rental charges incurred when you rent an auto from a rental agency or auto repair shop due to a loss to a covered auto for which Rental Reimbursement Coverage has been purchased. This coverage applies only if you have purchased both Comprehensive Coverage and Collision Coverage for that covered auto and the loss is covered under one of those coverages.

Additional fees or charges for insurance, damage waivers, optional equipment, fuel, or accessories are not covered.

This coverage is limited to the each day limit shown on the declarations page for a maximum of 30 days.

If  Rental Reimbursement Coverage applies, no other coverage under this policy for rental expenses will apply .

## Rental charges will be reimbursed beginning:

- 1 . when the covered auto cannot be driven due to a loss; or
2. if the covered auto can be driven, when you deliver the covered auto to an auto repair shop or one of our Service Centers for repairs due to the loss; and ending the earliest of:
- 1 . when the covered auto has been returned to you ;
2. when the covered auto has been repaired;
3. when the covered auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the covered auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or
5. when you incur 30 days worth of rental charges.

You must provide us written proof of your rental charges to be reimbursed.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-LOAN/LEASE PAYOFF COVERAGE

1|INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community|"# INSURER and INSURED PERSON: The Auto Insurance Policy Community

The community centers on the relationship between the INSURER and the INSURED PERSON, with the INSURANCE POLICY as the governing contract. The policy is structured into three main coverage parts: Part I-Liability to Others, Part II-Medical Payments Coverage, and Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage. Various entities such as RELATIVE, LIABLE PARTY, MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDER, and ATTOTNEY interact with these core parties, creating a network of rights, obligations, and potential disputes. The community is characterized by complex legal and financial relationships, with the INSURER holding rights of recovery and the INSURED PERSON entitled to benefits but also subject to reimbursement and cooperation requirements. The presence of arbitration, financial responsibility laws, and material misrepresentation clauses adds layers of regulatory and legal significance.

## Central relationship between INSURER and INSURED PERSON

The INSURER and INSURED PERSON form the core of the insurance community. The INSURER provides financial protection, makes payments on behalf of the insured, and retains rights of recovery and reimbursement. The INSURED PERSON is entitled to benefits such as medical payments and liability coverage, but must also cooperate with the insurer, sign documents, and reimburse payments from liable parties. This relationship is fundamental to the operation of the policy and underlies all other interactions. [Data: Entities (71, 68); Relationships (90, 77, 120, 122, 310, 318, 319, +more)]

## Insurance policy structure and coverage parts

The INSURANCE POLICY is the contract that binds the parties and is divided into three main parts. Part I-Liability to Others covers the insured's liability to third parties, with the insurer's duty to pay contingent on a final determination of the insured's obligation. Part II-Medical Payments Coverage provides for medical expenses due to bodily injury from auto accidents. Part III-Uninsured/Underinsured Motorist Coverage addresses situations where the other driver is uninsured or underinsured, and may reduce payments under Part I. These parts define the scope of coverage and the conditions under which benefits are paid. [Data: Entities (75, 3, 83, 84, 85); Relationships (106, 158, 18, 19, +more)]

## DEFINITIONS OF LIABLE PARTY AND RECOVERY RIGHTS

The LIABLE PARTY is an entity or individual legally or financially obligated to make payments to an insured person. The insured person may recover from the liable party, and such amounts are held in trust for the insurer. The INSURER holds RECOVERY RIGHTS to the extent of its payments, and the insured must assist in exercising these rights. This dynamic creates a triangular relationship where the insurer seeks reimbursement from the liable party, often requiring the insured's cooperation. [Data: Entities (181, 187, 188); Relationships (310, 319, 320)]

## ROLE OF MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS AND ATTORNEYS

MEDICAL SERVICE PROVIDERS deliver medical services and may sue the insured person if the insurer refuses to pay for expenses deemed unreasonable or unnecessary. They may also pursue collection activities. ATTORNEYS represent insured persons in recovering payments from liable parties, with fees shared pro rata by the insurer. These entities introduce potential legal disputes and financial obligations that can escalate the complexity of claims. [Data: Entities (88, 182); Relationships (135, 312)]

## RELATIVE AND RATED RESIDENT AS INSURED PERSONS

A RELATIVE is defined as a family member related by blood, marriage, or adoption, and may qualify as an insured person under the policy, particularly for accidents arising from the ownership, maintenance, or use of an auto. A RATED RESIDENT is included within the definition of an insured person and is covered for auto-related accidents. However, coverage can be affected by factors such as the relative's driver's license status, vehicle ownership or regular use, and intentional acts. These entities expand the scope of who is protected under the policy. [Data: Entities (63, 68); Relationships (77, 110)]

## ARBITRATION AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

ARBITRATION is a subsection of Part III and is used to determine the legal liability of the operator or owner of an uninsured motor vehicle and the amount of damages sustained by the insured person. Each party selects an arbitrator, and the two arbitrators select a third. The court may appoint the third arbitrator on joint application. This mechanism provides an alternative to litigation for resolving disputes related to uninsured or underinsured motorist claims. [Data: Entities (26, 103, 104); Relationships (34, 167, 166)]

## MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION AND CANCELLATION

MATERIAL MISREPRESENTATION is a misrepresentation of a material fact in the procurement, continuation, change, or renewal of the policy, or in the submission of a claim, which constitutes grounds for cancellation after 59 days. This clause protects the insurer from fraud and ensures that the policy is based on accurate information. The insured person's obligation to provide truthful information is thus critical to maintaining coverage. [Data: Entities (173, 184, 70); Relationships (277, 314, 315)]

## FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS AND OTHER LEGAL REQUIREMENTS

FINANCIAL RESPONSIBILITY LAWS are a subsection of Part I-Liability to Others and mandate that individuals demonstrate the ability to cover damages arising from vehicle accidents, typically through insurance. A policy complies with these laws when properly certified. Additionally, sums paid under workers' compensation or disability benefits laws reduce the limits of liability under Part III. These legal requirements ensure that insured persons meet statutory obligations and that the insurer's liability is coordinated with other sources of compensation. [Data: Entities (21, 99, 100); Relationships (126, 161, 162)]"

## UNREASONABLE OR UNNECESSARY MEDICAL EXPENSES

If an insured person incurs expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we may refuse to pay for those expenses and contest them.

If the medical service provider sues the insured person because we refuse to pay expenses for medical services that we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary, we will pay any resulting defense costs, and any resulting judgment against the insured person , subject to the limit of liability for this coverage. We will choose the counsel. We will also pay reasonable expenses, including loss of earnings up to $200 per day, incurred at our request.

The insured person may not sue us for expenses for medical services we deem to be unreasonable or unnecessary unless the insured person paid the entire disputed amount to the medical service provider or the medical service provider has initiated collection activity against the insured person for the unreasonable or unnecessary expenses.

## OTHER INSURANCE

If there is other applicable auto medical payments insurance, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable limits. However, any insurance we provide for an insured person occupying a vehicle or trailer, other than a covered auto , will be excess over any other auto insurance providing payments for medical services .

At our expense, we may return any recovered stolen property to you or to the address shown on the declarations page , with payment for any damage resulting from the theft. We may keep all or part of the property at the agreed or appraised value.

We may settle any loss with you or the owner or lienholder of the property .

## NO BENEFIT TO BAILEE

Coverage under this Part IV will not directly or indirectly benefit any carrier or other bailee for hire.

## LOSS PAYABLE CLAUSE

Payment under this Part IV for a loss to a covered auto will be made according to your interest and the interest of any lienholder shown on the declarations page or designated by you .  At our option, payment may be made to both jointly, or to either separately. However, if the covered auto is not a total loss, we may make payment to you and the repairer of the auto .

The lienholder's interest will not be protected:

- 1 . where fraud, misrepresentation, material omission, or intentional damage resulting in a denial of coverage by us has been committed by or at the direction of you or any person seeking coverage; or
2. where the loss is otherwise not covered under the terms of this policy .

If this policy is cancelled, nonrenewed or voided, the interest of any lienholder under this agreement will also terminate.

## OTHER SOURCES OF RECOVERY

If other sources of recovery also cover the loss, we will pay only our share of the loss. Our share is the proportion that our limit of liability bears to the total of all applicable

limits. However, any insurance we provide for a non-owned auto , or trailer not shown on the declarations page , will be excess over any other collectible source of recovery including, but not limited to:

- 1 . any coverage provided by the owner of the non-owned auto or trailer ;
2. any other applicable physical damage insurance; and
3. any other source of recovery applicable to the loss.

## APPRAISAL

If we cannot agree with you on the amount of a loss, then we or you may demand an appraisal of the loss. Within 30 days of any demand for an appraisal, each party shall appoint a competent appraiser and shall notify the other party of that appraiser's identity . The appraisers will determine the amount of loss. If they fail to agree, the disagreement will be submitted to a qualified umpire chosen by the appraisers. If the two appraisers are unable to agree upon an umpire within 15 days, we or you may request that a judge of a court of record, in the county where you reside, select an umpire. The appraisers and umpire will determine the amount of loss. The amount of loss agreed to by both appraisers, or by one appraiser and the umpire, will be binding. You will pay your appraiser's fees and expenses. We will pay our appraiser's fees and expenses. All other expenses of the appraisal, including payment of the umpire if one is selected, will be shared equally between us and you .   Neither we nor you waive any rights under this policy by agreeing to an appraisal.

## INSURING AGREEMENT

If you pay the premium for this coverage, we will pay for our authorized service representative to provide the following services when necessary due to a covered emergency :

- 1 . towing of a covered disabled auto to the nearest qualified repair facility; and
2. labor on a covered disabled auto at the place of disablement.

If a covered disabled auto is towed to any place other than the nearest qualified repair facility , you will be responsible for any additional charges incurred.

## INSURING AGREEMENT-COMPREHENSIVE COVERAGE

- 1 . covered auto , including an attached trailer ; or
2. non-owned auto ;

and its custom parts or equipment , that is not caused by collision .

## A loss not caused by collision includes:

- 1 . contact with an animal (including a bird);
2. explosion or earthquake;
3. fire;
4. malicious mischief or vandalism;

The additional benefit for transportation expenses will not apply if you purchased Rental Reimbursement Coverage for the stolen covered auto .

Coverage for transportation expenses and loss of use damages begins 48 hours after you report the theft to us and ends the earliest of:

- 1 . when the auto has been recovered and returned to you or its owner;
2. when the auto has been recovered and repaired;
3. when the auto has been replaced;
4. 72 hours after we make an offer to settle the loss if the auto is deemed by us to be a total loss; or

In return for your payment of the premium, we agree to insure you subject to all the terms, conditions and limitations of this policy . ## CHANGES

This policy contract, your insurance application (which is made a part of this policy as if attached hereto), the declarations page , and all endorsements to this policy issued by us , contain all the agreements between you and us .   Subject to the following, the terms of this policy may not be changed or waived except by an endorsement issued by us .

The premium for this policy is based on information we received from you and other sources. You agree to cooperate with us in determining if this information is correct and complete, and to promptly notify us if it changes during the policy period. If this information is determined by us to be incorrect, incomplete, or if it changes during the policy period, you agree that we may adjust your policy information and premium accordingly. Changes that may result in a premium adjustment are contained in our rates and rules. These include, but are not limited to, you , a relative , or a rated resident obtaining a driver's license or operator's permit, or changes in:

- 1 . the number, type or use classification of covered autos ;
2. the persons who regularly operate a covered auto ;
3. the persons of legal driving age residing in your household;
4. the residents in your household;
5. an operator's marital status;
6. your mailing address and your residence address;
- 7 . the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
8. coverage, deductibles, or limits of liability; or
9. rating territory or discount eligibility .

The coverage provided in your policy may be changed only by the issuance of a new policy or an endorsement by us .  However, if during the policy period we broaden any coverage afforded under the current edition of your policy without additional premium charge, that change will automatically apply to your policy as of the date the coverage change is implemented in your state.

If you ask us to delete a vehicle from this policy , no coverage will apply to that vehicle as of the date and time you ask us to delete it.

## DUTY TO REPORT CHANGES

You must promptly report to us all changes, including additions and deletions, in policy information. This includes, but is not limited to, changes in:

- 1 . your mailing address or your residence address;
2. the principal garaging address of any covered auto ;
3. the residents in your household;
4. the persons of legal driving age residing in your household;
5. the persons who regularly operate a covered auto ;
6. an operator's marital status; or
- 7 . the driver's license or operator's permit status of you , a relative , or a rated resident.

## SETTLEMENT OF CLAIMS

We may use estimating, appraisal, or injury evaluation systems to assist us in adjusting claims under this policy and to assist us in determining the amount of damages, expenses, or loss payable under this policy . Such systems may be developed by us or a third party and may include computer software, databases, and specialized technology.

## TERMS OF POLICY CONFORMED TO STATUTES

If any provision of this policy fails to conform to the statutes of the state listed on your application as your residence, the provision shall be deemed amended to conform to such statutes. All other provisions shall be given full force and effect. Any disputes as to the coverages provided or the provisions of this policy shall be governed by the law of the state listed on your application as your residence.

## TRANSFER OF INTEREST

The rights and duties under this policy may not be transferred to another person without our written consent. However, if a named insured shown on the declarations page dies, this policy will provide coverage until the end of the policy period for the legal representative of the named insured, while acting as such, and for persons covered under this policy on the date of the named insured's death.

## FRAUD OR MISREPRESENTATION

Any changes we make at your request to this policy after inception will be made in reliance upon information you provide. If you :

- 1 . make incorrect statements or representations to us with regard to any material fact or circumstance;
2. conceal or misrepresent any material fact or circumstance; or
3. engage in fraudulent conduct;

we may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you , in connection with any requested change, or at any time during the policy period, have concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance or engaged in fraudulent conduct and that concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct was material to a risk we assumed.

We may deny coverage for an accident or loss if you or a person seeking coverage has concealed or misrepresented any material fact or circumstance, or engaged in fraudulent conduct which materially affects our interests, in connection with the presentation or settlement of a claim.

## PAYMENT OF PREMIUM AND FEES

In addition to premium, fees may be charged on your policy . We may charge fees for installment payments, late payments, and other transactions. Fees may also be charged if you tender a check, draft, electronic funds transfer, or other type of remittance to us for any full or partial payment of your premium, and the method of such payment is returned to us or refused because of insufficient funds, a closed account, or a stop payment order. Payments made on your policy will be applied first to fees, then to premium due.

We may cancel this policy during the policy period by mailing a notice of cancellation to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records.

"Fraud or Misrepresentation" is a policy provision event that addresses concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct, all of which may lead to the denial of coverage. It is also designated as a subsection of Part VII – General Provisions, where it formally governs matters of fraud or misrepresentation within the broader policy framework.

In essence, this provision serves a dual role: it identifies specific types of conduct—concealment, misrepresentation, and fraud—as events that can trigger adverse consequences for the insured, and it situates that treatment within the General Provisions section of the policy. The central consequence associated with this provision is the potential denial of coverage, underscoring its importance as a mechanism for protecting the insurer against claims arising from dishonest or misleading conduct.

Because the two descriptions refer to the same entity and are complementary rather than contradictory, they can be read together: "Fraud or Misrepresentation" is both a substantive policy provision event and a formal subsection of Part VII – General Provisions, united by their shared focus on concealment, misrepresentation, or fraudulent conduct and the resulting possibility that coverage may be denied.|2

## CANCELLATION REFUND

Upon cancellation, you may be entitled to a premium refund. However, our making or offering of a refund is not a condition of cancellation.

If this policy is cancelled, any refund due will be computed on a daily pro rata basis. However, we will retain a cancellation fee if this policy is cancelled at your request or if cancellation is for nonpayment of premium. A cancellation fee will be charged only during the initial policy period.

## NONRENEWAL

If neither we nor one of our affiliates offers to renew or continue this policy , we will mail notice of nonrenewal to the named insured shown on the declarations page at the last known address appearing in our records. A postal service certificate of mailing to the named insured at the insured's last known address appearing in our records will be sufficient proof of notice. Notice will be mailed more than 33 days before the end of the policy period.

## AUTOMATIC TERMINATION

If we or an affiliate offers to renew or continue this policy and you or your representative does not accept, this policy will automatically terminate at the end of the current policy period. Failure to pay the required renewal or continuation premium when due will mean that you have not accepted our offer.

If you obtain other insurance on a covered auto , any similar insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the other insurance.

If a covered auto is sold or transferred to someone other than you or a relative , any insurance provided by this policy will terminate as to that covered auto on the effective date of the sale or transfer.

## LEGAL ACTION AGAINST US

We may not be sued unless there is full compliance with all the terms of this policy .

We may not be sued for payment under Part I-Liability T o Others until the obligation of an insured person under Part I to pay is finally determined either by judgment after trial against that person or by written agreement of the insured person, the claimant, and us . No one will have any right to make us a party to a lawsuit to determine the liability of an insured person.

If we retain salvage, we have no duty to preserve or otherwise retain the salvage for any purpose, including evidence for any civil or criminal proceeding.

## OUR RIGHTS TO RECOVER PAYMENT

We are entitled to the rights of recovery that the insured person to whom payment was made has against another, to the extent of our payment. That insured person may be required to sign documents related to the recovery and must do whatever else we require to help us exercise those recovery rights, and do nothing after an accident or loss to prejudice those rights.

When an insured person has been paid by us and also recovers from another, the amount recovered will be held by the insured person in trust for us and reimbursed to

us to the extent of our payment. If we are not reimbursed, we may pursue recovery of that amount directly against that insured person.

2. we are responsible for a pro rata share of the attorney fees incurred by that insured person in recovering payment from a liable party.

If an insured person recovers from another without our written consent, and such recovery prejudices our right to recover payment, the insured person's right to payment under any affected coverage will no longer exist.
